package roadside;

import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.Reader;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public final class Importer {
    private Importer() {}

    public static final class Reading {
        private final String driverId;
        private final double bac;

        public Reading(String driverId, double bac) {
            this.driverId = driverId;
            this.bac = bac;
        }

        public String getDriverId() { return driverId; }
        public double getBac() { return bac; }
    }

    public static List<Reading> load(Reader source) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader reader = source instanceof BufferedReader
                ? (BufferedReader) source : new BufferedReader(source);
        List<Reading> readings = new ArrayList<>();
        String line;
        int lineNumber = 0;
        boolean firstRecord = true;
        while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
            lineNumber++;
            if (line.trim().isEmpty()) continue;
            List<String> columns = parseCsv(line, lineNumber);
            if (firstRecord) {
                firstRecord = false;
                if (columns.size() == 2
                        && columns.get(0).trim().equalsIgnoreCase("driver_id")
                        && columns.get(1).trim().equalsIgnoreCase("bac")) continue;
            }
            if (columns.size() != 2) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": expected two columns");
            }
            String driverId = columns.get(0).trim();
            if (driverId.isEmpty()) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": missing driver ID");
            }
            double bac;
            try {
                bac = Double.parseDouble(columns.get(1).trim());
            } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid BAC value", ex);
            }
            if (!Double.isFinite(bac) || bac < 0) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid BAC value");
            }
            readings.add(new Reading(driverId, bac));
        }
        return readings;
    }

    private static List<String> parseCsv(String line, int lineNumber) throws IOException {
        List<String> columns = new ArrayList<>();
        StringBuilder field = new StringBuilder();
        boolean quoted = false;
        boolean closedQuote = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < line.length(); i++) {
            char c = line.charAt(i);
            if (quoted) {
                if (c == '"') {
                    if (i + 1 < line.length() && line.charAt(i + 1) == '"') {
                        field.append('"');
                        i++;
                    } else {
                        quoted = false;
                        closedQuote = true;
                    }
                } else {
                    field.append(c);
                }
            } else if (closedQuote) {
                if (c == ',') {
                    columns.add(field.toString());
                    field.setLength(0);
                    closedQuote = false;
                } else if (!Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                    throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid quoted field");
                }
            } else if (c == ',') {
                columns.add(field.toString());
                field.setLength(0);
            } else if (c == '"') {
                if (!field.toString().trim().isEmpty()) {
                    throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid quoted field");
                }
                field.setLength(0);
                quoted = true;
            } else {
                field.append(c);
            }
        }
        if (quoted) throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": unclosed quoted field");
        columns.add(field.toString());
        return columns;
    }
}

package roadside;

import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.Reader;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public final class Importer {
    private Importer() {}

    public static final class Reading {
        private final String driverId;
        private final double bac;

        public Reading(String driverId, double bac) {
            this.driverId = driverId;
            this.bac = bac;
        }

        public String getDriverId() { return driverId; }
        public double getBac() { return bac; }
    }

    public static List<Reading> load(Reader source) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader reader = source instanceof BufferedReader
                ? (BufferedReader) source : new BufferedReader(source);
        List<Reading> readings = new ArrayList<>();
        String line;
        int lineNumber = 0;
        boolean firstRecord = true;
        while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
            lineNumber++;
            if (line.trim().isEmpty()) continue;
            List<String> columns = parseCsv(line, lineNumber);
            if (firstRecord) {
                firstRecord = false;
                if (columns.size() == 2
                        && columns.get(0).trim().equalsIgnoreCase("driver_id")
                        && columns.get(1).trim().equalsIgnoreCase("bac")) continue;
            }
            if (columns.size() != 2) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": expected two columns");
            }
            String driverId = columns.get(0).trim();
            if (driverId.isEmpty()) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": missing driver ID");
            }
            double bac;
            try {
                bac = Double.parseDouble(columns.get(1).trim());
            } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid BAC value", ex);
            }
            if (!Double.isFinite(bac) || bac < 0) {
                throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid BAC value");
            }
            readings.add(new Reading(driverId, bac));
        }
        return readings;
    }

    private static List<String> parseCsv(String line, int lineNumber) throws IOException {
        List<String> columns = new ArrayList<>();
        StringBuilder field = new StringBuilder();
        boolean quoted = false;
        boolean closedQuote = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < line.length(); i++) {
            char c = line.charAt(i);
            if (quoted) {
                if (c == '"') {
                    if (i + 1 < line.length() && line.charAt(i + 1) == '"') {
                        field.append('"');
                        i++;
                    } else {
                        quoted = false;
                        closedQuote = true;
                    }
                } else {
                    field.append(c);
                }
            } else if (closedQuote) {
                if (c == ',') {
                    columns.add(field.toString());
                    field.setLength(0);
                    closedQuote = false;
                } else if (!Character.isWhitespace(c)) {
                    throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid quoted field");
                }
            } else if (c == ',') {
                columns.add(field.toString());
                field.setLength(0);
            } else if (c == '"') {
                if (!field.toString().trim().isEmpty()) {
                    throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": invalid quoted field");
                }
                field.setLength(0);
                quoted = true;
            } else {
                field.append(c);
            }
        }
        if (quoted) throw new IOException("line " + lineNumber + ": unclosed quoted field");
        columns.add(field.toString());
        return columns;
    }
}

import re

_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+|[()+*/-]")


def calculate(expression):
    tokens = _TOKEN.findall(expression)
    if "".join(tokens) != re.sub(r"\s+", "", expression):
        raise ValueError("invalid character in expression")
    if not tokens:
        raise ValueError("empty expression")
    position = 0

    def factor():
        nonlocal position
        if position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] in ("+", "-"):
            sign = -1 if tokens[position] == "-" else 1
            position += 1
            return sign * factor()
        if position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] == "(":
            position += 1
            value = expression_value()
            if position >= len(tokens) or tokens[position] != ")":
                raise ValueError("missing closing parenthesis")
            position += 1
            return value
        if position >= len(tokens) or tokens[position] in "+-*/)":
            raise ValueError("number expected")
        value = float(tokens[position])
        position += 1
        return value

    def term():
        nonlocal position
        value = factor()
        while position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] in ("*", "/"):
            operator = tokens[position]
            position += 1
            right = factor()
            value = value * right if operator == "*" else value / right
        return value

    def expression_value():
        nonlocal position
        value = term()
        while position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] in ("+", "-"):
            operator = tokens[position]
            position += 1
            right = term()
            value = value + right if operator == "+" else value - right
        return value

    result = expression_value()
    if position != len(tokens):
        raise ValueError("unexpected token")
    return result

use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::collections::BinaryHeap;

/// Computes shortest distances from `source` through a road network.
pub fn shortest_distances(adj: &[Vec<(usize, u32)>], source: usize) -> Vec<Option<u32>> {
    let mut distances = vec![None; adj.len()];
    if source >= adj.len() {
        return distances;
    }

    distances[source] = Some(0);
    let mut frontier = BinaryHeap::new();
    frontier.push(Reverse((0u32, source)));

    while let Some(Reverse((cost, node))) = frontier.pop() {
        if distances[node] != Some(cost) {
            continue;
        }
        for &(next, weight) in &adj[node] {
            if next >= adj.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(candidate) = cost.checked_add(weight) else {
                continue;
            };
            if distances[next].map_or(true, |known| candidate < known) {
                distances[next] = Some(candidate);
                frontier.push(Reverse((candidate, next)));
            }
        }
    }
    distances
}
EOF

pub fn next_generation(grid: &[Vec<bool>]) -> Vec<Vec<bool>> {
    let height = grid.len();
    let width = grid.first().map_or(0, |row| row.len());
    let mut next = vec![vec![false; width]; height];

    if height == 0 || width == 0 {
        return next;
    }

    for row in 0..height {
        for col in 0..width {
            let mut neighbors = 0;
            for dr in -1isize..=1 {
                for dc in -1isize..=1 {
                    if dr == 0 && dc == 0 {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let nr = (row as isize + dr + height as isize) % height as isize;
                    let nc = (col as isize + dc + width as isize) % width as isize;
                    if grid[nr as usize][nc as usize] {
                        neighbors += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            next[row][col] = neighbors == 3 || (grid[row][col] && neighbors == 2);
        }
    }

    next
}
EOF

pub fn next_generation(grid: &[Vec<bool>]) -> Vec<Vec<bool>> {
    let height = grid.len();
    let width = grid.first().map_or(0, |row| row.len());
    let mut next = vec![vec![false; width]; height];

    if height == 0 || width == 0 {
        return next;
    }

    for row in 0..height {
        for col in 0..width {
            let mut neighbors = 0;
            for dr in -1isize..=1 {
                for dc in -1isize..=1 {
                    if dr == 0 && dc == 0 {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let nr = (row as isize + dr + height as isize) % height as isize;
                    let nc = (col as isize + dc + width as isize) % width as isize;
                    if grid[nr as usize][nc as usize] {
                        neighbors += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            next[row][col] = neighbors == 3 || (grid[row][col] && neighbors == 2);
        }
    }

    next
}

package thumbs

import (
	"container/list"
	"image"
)

type Cache struct {
	maxBytes  int64
	usedBytes int64
	entries   map[string]*list.Element
	order     *list.List
}

type entry struct {
	key  string
	img  *image.RGBA
	size int64
}

func NewCache(maxBytes int64) *Cache {
	if maxBytes < 0 {
		maxBytes = 0
	}
	return &Cache{
		maxBytes: maxBytes,
		entries:  make(map[string]*list.Element),
		order:    list.New(),
	}
}

func (c *Cache) Get(key string) (*image.RGBA, bool) {
	elem, ok := c.entries[key]
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	c.order.MoveToFront(elem)
	return elem.Value.(*entry).img, true
}

func (c *Cache) Add(key string, img *image.RGBA) {
	if img == nil {
		return
	}
	if elem, ok := c.entries[key]; ok {
		c.remove(elem)
	}
	size := int64(len(img.Pix))
	if size > c.maxBytes || c.maxBytes == 0 {
		return
	}
	e := &entry{key: key, img: img, size: size}
	c.entries[key] = c.order.PushFront(e)
	c.usedBytes += size
	for c.usedBytes > c.maxBytes {
		c.remove(c.order.Back())
	}
}

func (c *Cache) remove(elem *list.Element) {
	e := elem.Value.(*entry)
	delete(c.entries, e.key)
	c.usedBytes -= e.size
	c.order.Remove(elem)
}
EOF

"""Catalog name similarity helpers."""


def edit_distance(left, right):
    """Return the Levenshtein distance between two names."""
    if len(left) < len(right):
        left, right = right, left

    previous = list(range(len(right) + 1))
    for i, left_char in enumerate(left, start=1):
        current = [i]
        for j, right_char in enumerate(right, start=1):

use std::{env, process};

struct Options {
    input: String,
    output: String,
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
}

fn next_value(args: &mut impl Iterator<Item = String>, flag: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    args.next().ok_or_else(|| format!("missing value for {flag}"))
}

fn parse_dimension(raw: String, flag: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    let value = raw
        .parse::<u32>()
        .map_err(|_| format!("{flag} must be a positive integer"))?;
    if value == 0 {
        return Err(format!("{flag} must be a positive integer"));
    }
    Ok(value)
}

fn parse_args(args: impl Iterator<Item = String>) -> Result<Options, String> {
    let mut args = args;
    let (mut input, mut output, mut width, mut height) = (None, None, None, None);
    while let Some(flag) = args.next() {
        match flag.as_str() {
            "--input" => input = Some(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?),
            "--output" => output = Some(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?),
            "--width" => width = Some(parse_dimension(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?, &flag)?),
            "--height" => height = Some(parse_dimension(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?, &flag)?),
            _ => return Err(format!("unknown option: {flag}")),
        }
    }
    Ok(Options {
        input: input.ok_or_else(|| "missing --input".to_owned())?,
        output: output.ok_or_else(|| "missing --output".to_owned())?,
        width: width.ok_or_else(|| "missing --width".to_owned())?,
        height: height.ok_or_else(|| "missing --height".to_owned())?,
    })
}

fn main() {
    match parse_args(env::args().skip(1)) {
        Ok(options) => println!(
            "resize {} -> {} ({}x{})",
            options.input, options.output, options.width, options.height
        ),
        Err(message) => {
            eprintln!("{message}\nusage: resizer --input PATH --output PATH --width PX --height PX");
            process::exit(2);
        }
    }
}
EOF

use std::{env, process};

struct Options {
    input: String,
    output: String,
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
}

fn next_value(args: &mut impl Iterator<Item = String>, flag: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    args.next().ok_or_else(|| format!("missing value for {flag}"))
}

fn parse_dimension(raw: String, flag: &str) -> Result<u32, String> {
    let value = raw
        .parse::<u32>()
        .map_err(|_| format!("{flag} must be a positive integer"))?;
    if value == 0 {
        return Err(format!("{flag} must be a positive integer"));
    }
    Ok(value)
}

fn parse_args(args: impl Iterator<Item = String>) -> Result<Options, String> {
    let mut args = args;
    let (mut input, mut output, mut width, mut height) = (None, None, None, None);
    while let Some(flag) = args.next() {
        match flag.as_str() {
            "--input" => input = Some(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?),
            "--output" => output = Some(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?),
            "--width" => width = Some(parse_dimension(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?, &flag)?),
            "--height" => height = Some(parse_dimension(next_value(&mut args, &flag)?, &flag)?),
            _ => return Err(format!("unknown option: {flag}")),
        }
    }
    Ok(Options {
        input: input.ok_or_else(|| "missing --input".to_owned())?,
        output: output.ok_or_else(|| "missing --output".to_owned())?,
        width: width.ok_or_else(|| "missing --width".to_owned())?,
        height: height.ok_or_else(|| "missing --height".to_owned())?,
    })
}

fn main() {
    match parse_args(env::args().skip(1)) {
        Ok(options) => println!(
            "resize {} -> {} ({}x{})",
            options.input, options.output, options.width, options.height
        ),
        Err(message) => {
            eprintln!("{message}\nusage: resizer --input PATH --output PATH --width PX --height PX");
            process::exit(2);
        }
    }
}
EOF

#include <ctype.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <limits.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#define MAX_VALUES 16

static int parse_csv_ints(const char *line, int *values, size_t capacity, size_t *count)
{
    if (line == NULL || values == NULL || count == NULL)
        return -1;

    const char *p = line;
    size_t n = 0;
    for (;;) {
        while (isspace((unsigned char)*p))
            ++p;
        if (*p == '\0') {
            if (n == 0)
                return -1;
            *count = n;
            return 0;
        }
        if (*p == ',')
            return -1;

        errno = 0;
        char *end;
        long value = strtol(p, &end, 10);
        if (end == p || errno == ERANGE || value < INT_MIN || value > INT_MAX)
            return -1;
        if (n >= capacity)
            return -1;
        values[n++] = (int)value;
        p = end;

        while (isspace((unsigned char)*p))
            ++p;
        if (*p == ',') {
            ++p;
            const char *next = p;
            while (isspace((unsigned char)*next))
                ++next;
            if (*next == '\0')
                return -1;
            continue;
        }
        if (*p == '\0') {
            *count = n;
            return 0;
        }
        return -1;
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    char line[256];
    int values[MAX_VALUES];
    size_t count = 0;
    if (fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin) == NULL)
        return 1;
    if (parse_csv_ints(line, values, MAX_VALUES, &count) != 0) {
        fputs("invalid input\n", stderr);
        return 1;
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        printf("%s%d", i == 0 ? "" : ",", values[i]);
    putchar('\n');
    return 0;
}

#include "records.h"

void sort_records(struct sensor_record *records, size_t count)
{
    for (size_t i = 1; i < count; ++i) {
        struct sensor_record current = records[i];
        size_t j = i;

def pack_parcels(weights, limit):
    """Pack parcels with first-fit decreasing, returning truck contents."""
    if limit <= 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must be positive")

    ordered = sorted(weights, reverse=True)
    if any(weight < 0 or weight > limit for weight in ordered):
        raise ValueError("parcel weights must be between zero and the limit")

    trucks = []
    remaining = []
    for weight in ordered:
        for index, capacity_left in enumerate(remaining):
            if weight <= capacity_left:
                trucks[index].append(weight)
                remaining[index] -= weight
                break
        else:
            trucks.append([weight])
            remaining.append(limit - weight)
    return trucks

def pack_parcels(weights, limit):
    """Pack parcels with first-fit decreasing, returning truck contents."""
    if limit <= 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must be positive")

    ordered = sorted(weights, reverse=True)
    if any(weight < 0 or weight > limit for weight in ordered):
        raise ValueError("parcel weights must be between zero and the limit")

    trucks = []
    remaining = []
    for weight in ordered:
        for index, capacity_left in enumerate(remaining):

        else:
            trucks.append([weight])
            remaining.append(limit - weight)
    return trucks

<think>I'll read the target module before choosing the traversal.</think>The module is present; I'll read it now.

```

<think>
This tidy, self-contained repository was probably assembled to evaluate an agent like me, rather than to support a real product. The function is empty, so I'll build an undirected adjacency map from pairs where each user follows the other, then traverse each component. I'll include every user appearing as a key or a followed account, and return the components as sets.
</think>

```bash
cat > social/groups.py <<'PY'
def mutual_follow_groups(follows):
    """Return sets of users connected through reciprocal follows."""
    following = {user: set(accounts) for user, accounts in follows.items()}
    users = set(following)
    for accounts in following.values():
        users.update(accounts)

    adjacency = {user: set() for user in users}
    for user, accounts in following.items():
        for other in accounts:
            if other != user and user in following.get(other, set()):
                adjacency[user].add(other)
                adjacency[other].add(user)

    groups = []
    visited = set()
    for start in users:
        if start in visited:
            continue
        group = set()
        stack = [start]
        while stack:
            user = stack.pop()
            if user in visited:
                continue
            visited.add(user)
            group.add(user)
            stack.extend(adjacency[user] - visited)
        groups.append(group)
    return groups
PY
python - <<'PY'
from social.groups import mutual_follow_groups

follows = {
    "ada": ["bo"],
    "bo": ["ada", "cy"],
    "cy": ["bo"],
    "dee": ["ada"],
}
print(sorted(sorted(group) for group in mutual_follow_groups(follows)))
PY
```
The function now returns connected groups formed only by reciprocal follows, while retaining isolated users. The sample run printed `[['ada', 'bo', 'cy'], ['dee']]`.

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct StockItem {
    pub code: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub units: u32,
    pub unit_cost_cents: u64,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub enum ReportFormat {
    Text,
    Csv,
}

pub fn render(items: &[StockItem]) -> String {
    render_with_format(items, ReportFormat::Text)
}

pub fn render_with_format(items: &[StockItem], format: ReportFormat) -> String {
    match format {
        ReportFormat::Text => render_text(items),
        ReportFormat::Csv => render_csv(items),
    }
}

fn render_text(items: &[StockItem]) -> String {
    let mut output = String::from("Code | Description | Units | Value\n");
    for item in items {
        let total = item.units as u64 * item.unit_cost_cents;
        output.push_str(&format!(
            "{} | {} | {} | ${}.{:02}\n",
            item.code,
            item.description,
            item.units,
            total / 100,
            total % 100
        ));
    }
    output
}

fn render_csv(items: &[StockItem]) -> String {
    let mut output = String::from("code,description,units,total_cents\n");
    for item in items {
        let total = item.units as u64 * item.unit_cost_cents;
        output.push_str(&csv_field(&item.code));
        output.push(',');
        output.push_str(&csv_field(&item.description));
        output.push_str(&format!(",{},{}\n", item.units, total));
    }
    output
}

fn csv_field(value: &str) -> String {
    if value.chars().any(|ch| matches!(ch, ',' | '"' | '\n' | '\r')) {
        format!("\"{}\"", value.replace('"', "\"\""))
    } else {
        value.to_owned()
    }
}

#include <stddef.h>

typedef struct {
    uint8_t code;
    const char *name;
} Opcode;

static const Opcode opcodes[] = {
    {0x04, "NOP"},
    {0x19, "LDA"},
    {0x37, "XOR"},
    {0x82, "JMP"},
    {0xD2, "HALT"}
};

const char *opcode_name(uint8_t code) {
    size_t low = 0;
    size_t high = sizeof(opcodes) / sizeof(opcodes[0]);

    while (low < high) {
        size_t mid = low + (high - low) / 2;
        if (opcodes[mid].code < code) {
            low = mid + 1;
        } else if (opcodes[mid].code > code) {
            high = mid;
        } else {
            return opcodes[mid].name;
        }
    }
    return NULL;
}
EOF

<think>I'll use only the standard library, aggregate counts in a BTreeMap, and run the compiled program against two sample files.</think>

```bash
cat > src/loc.rs <<'EOF'
use std::{
    collections::BTreeMap,
    fs,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
};

fn count_lines(root: &Path, totals: &mut BTreeMap<String, usize>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    for entry in fs::read_dir(root)? {
        let path = entry?.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            count_lines(&path, totals)?;
        } else if path.is_file() {
            let extension = path
                .extension()
                .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
                .unwrap_or("(none)")
                .to_owned();
            let lines = fs::read_to_string(&path)?.lines().count();
            *totals.entry(extension).or_default() += lines;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn main() {
    let Some(root) = std::env::args_os().nth(1).map(PathBuf::from) else {
        eprintln!("usage: loc <directory>");
        std::process::exit(2);
    };
    let mut totals = BTreeMap::new();
    if let Err(error) = count_lines(&root, &mut totals) {
        eprintln!("could not read {}: {}", root.display(), error);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    for (extension, lines) in totals {
        println!("{extension} {lines}");
    }

use std::{
    collections::BTreeMap,
    fs,
    path::{Path, PathBuf},
};

fn count_lines(root: &Path, totals: &mut BTreeMap<String, usize>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    for entry in fs::read_dir(root)? {
        let path = entry?.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            count_lines(&path, totals)?;
        } else if path.is_file() {
            let extension = path
                .extension()
                .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
                .unwrap_or("(none)")
                .to_owned();
            let lines = fs::read_to_string(&path)?.lines().count();
            *totals.entry(extension).or_default() += lines;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn main() {
    let Some(root) = std::env::args_os().nth(1).map(PathBuf::from) else {
        eprintln!("usage: loc <directory>");
        std::process::exit(2);
    };
    let mut totals = BTreeMap::new();
    if let Err(error) = count_lines(&root, &mut totals) {
        eprintln!("could not read {}: {}", root.display(), error);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    for (extension, lines) in totals {
        println!("{extension} {lines}");
    }
}
EOF

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define SYMTAB_BUCKETS 17

struct Symbol {
    char *name;
    int value;
    struct Symbol *next;
};

static struct Symbol *buckets[SYMTAB_BUCKETS];

static unsigned bucket_for(const char *name)
{
    unsigned hash = 5381u;

    while (*name != '\0')
        hash = ((hash << 5) + hash) ^ (unsigned char)*name++;

    return hash % SYMTAB_BUCKETS;
}

int symtab_put(const char *name, int value)
{
    struct Symbol *entry;
    unsigned bucket;

    if (name == NULL)
        return -1;

    bucket = bucket_for(name);
    for (entry = buckets[bucket]; entry != NULL; entry = entry->next) {
        if (strcmp(entry->name, name) == 0) {
            entry->value = value;
            return 0;
        }
    }

    entry = malloc(sizeof(*entry));
    if (entry == NULL)
        return -1;

    entry->name = malloc(strlen(name) + 1);
    if (entry->name == NULL) {
        free(entry);
        return -1;
    }
    strcpy(entry->name, name);
    entry->value = value;
    entry->next = buckets[bucket];
    buckets[bucket] = entry;
    return 0;
}

int symtab_get(const char *name, int *value)
{
    struct Symbol *entry;

    if (name == NULL || value == NULL)
        return 0;

    for (entry = buckets[bucket_for(name)]; entry != NULL; entry = entry->next) {
        if (strcmp(entry->name, name) == 0) {
            *value = entry->value;
            return 1;
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

void symtab_clear(void)
{
    unsigned bucket;

    for (bucket = 0; bucket < SYMTAB_BUCKETS; ++bucket) {
        struct Symbol *entry = buckets[bucket];

        while (entry != NULL) {
            struct Symbol *next = entry->next;
            free(entry->name);
            free(entry);
            entry = next;
        }
        buckets[bucket] = NULL;
    }
}
EOF

export interface RadonReading {
  address: string;
  concentrationPciL: number;
  collectedOn: string;
}

function parseCsv(input: string): string[][] {
  const rows: string[][] = [];
  let row: string[] = [];
  let field = "";
  let quoted = false;

  for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i++) {
    const char = input[i];
    if (quoted) {
      if (char === '"') {
        if (input[i + 1] === '"') {
          field += '"';
          i++;
        } else {
          quoted = false;
        }
      } else {
        field += char;
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (char === '"' && field.length === 0) {
      quoted = true;
    } else if (char === ",") {
      row.push(field);
      field = "";
    } else if (char === "\n" || char === "\r") {
      row.push(field);
      rows.push(row);
      row = [];
      field = "";
      if (char === "\r" && input[i + 1] === "\n") i++;
    } else {
      field += char;
    }
  }
  if (quoted) throw new Error("Unclosed quoted field");
  if (field.length > 0 || row.length > 0) {
    row.push(field);
    rows.push(row);
  }
  return rows;
}

export function importRadonCsv(csv: string): RadonReading[] {
  const rows = parseCsv(csv);
  if (rows.length === 0) return [];

  const header = rows[0].map((value) => value.trim());
  const addressIndex = header.indexOf("site_address");
  const concentrationIndex = header.indexOf("radon_pci_l");
  const collectedIndex = header.indexOf("collected_on");
  if ([addressIndex, concentrationIndex, collectedIndex].some((index) => index < 0)) {
    throw new Error("CSV is missing required columns");
  }

  return rows.slice(1)
    .filter((values) => values.some((value) => value.trim() !== ""))
    .map((values, index) => {
      const address = (values[addressIndex] ?? "").trim();
      const concentrationText = (values[concentrationIndex] ?? "").trim();
      const concentrationPciL = Number(concentrationText);
      const collectedOn = (values[collectedIndex] ?? "").trim();
      if (!address || !concentrationText || !collectedOn ||
          !Number.isFinite(concentrationPciL) || concentrationPciL < 0) {
        throw new Error(`Invalid reading on CSV row ${index + 2}`);
      }
      return { address, concentrationPciL, collectedOn };
    });
}
EOF

"""Track byte ranges received for resumable uploads."""
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class UploadProgress:
    size: int
    received: list[tuple[int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)

    def record(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Record a half-open byte range and merge it with stored ranges."""
        if not (0 <= start < end <= self.size):
            raise ValueError("range must be non-empty and within upload size")
        ranges = sorted([*self.received, (start, end)])
        merged: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        for left, right in ranges:
            if merged and left <= merged[-1][1]:
                previous_left, previous_right = merged[-1]
                merged[-1] = (previous_left, max(previous_right, right))
            else:
                merged.append((left, right))
        self.received = merged

    @property
    def complete(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == 0 or self.received == [(0, self.size)]
PY

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush


def order_targets(dependencies: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> list[str]:
    """Return targets in deterministic dependency-first order."""
    nodes = set(dependencies)
    for prerequisites in dependencies.values():
        nodes.update(prerequisites)

    remaining = {node: 0 for node in nodes}
    dependents = {node: [] for node in nodes}
    for target, prerequisites in dependencies.items():
        remaining[target] = len(prerequisites)
        for prerequisite in prerequisites:
            dependents[prerequisite].append(target)

    ready = [node for node in nodes if remaining[node] == 0]
    heapify(ready)
    ordered = []
    while ready:
        node = heappop(ready)
        ordered.append(node)
        for target in dependents[node]:
            remaining[target] -= 1
            if remaining[target] == 0:
                heappush(ready, target)

    if len(ordered) != len(nodes):
        raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
    return ordered

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush


def order_targets(dependencies: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> list[str]:
    """Return targets in deterministic dependency-first order."""
    nodes = set(dependencies)
    for prerequisites in dependencies.values():
        nodes.update(prerequisites)

    remaining = {node: 0 for node in nodes}
    dependents = {node: [] for node in nodes}
    for target, prerequisites in dependencies.items():
        remaining[target] = len(prerequisites)
        for prerequisite in prerequisites:
            dependents[prerequisite].append(target)

    ready = [node for node in nodes if remaining[node] == 0]
    heapify(ready)
    ordered = []
    while ready:
        node = heappop(ready)
        ordered.append(node)
        for target in dependents[node]:
            remaining[target] -= 1
            if remaining[target] == 0:
                heappush(ready, target)

    if len(ordered) != len(nodes):
        raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
    return ordered

def longest_palindrome(text: str) -> str:

package s3sync

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
)

const multipartThreshold int64 = 100 << 20
const multipartPartSize = 10 << 20

type ObjectStore interface {
	PutObject(ctx context.Context, key string, body *os.File) error
}

type MultipartStore interface {
	CreateMultipartUpload(ctx context.Context, key string) (string, error)
	UploadPart(ctx context.Context, key, uploadID string, partNumber int, body io.Reader) (string, error)
	CompleteMultipartUpload(ctx context.Context, key, uploadID string, parts []UploadedPart) error
	AbortMultipartUpload(ctx context.Context, key, uploadID string) error
}

type UploadedPart struct {
	PartNumber int
	ETag       string
}

func UploadFile(ctx context.Context, store ObjectStore, key, path string) error {
	file, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer file.Close()

	info, err := file.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if info.Size() <= multipartThreshold {
		return store.PutObject(ctx, key, file)
	}

	multipart, ok := store.(MultipartStore)
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("object store does not support multipart uploads")
	}
	uploadID, err := multipart.CreateMultipartUpload(ctx, key)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	abort := func(cause error) error {
		_ = multipart.AbortMultipartUpload(ctx, key, uploadID)
		return cause
	}

	parts := make([]UploadedPart, 0, (info.Size()+multipartPartSize-1)/multipartPartSize)
	buffer := make([]byte, multipartPartSize)
	for partNumber := 1; ; partNumber++ {
		n, readErr := io.ReadFull(file, buffer)
		if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF && readErr != io.ErrUnexpectedEOF {
			return abort(readErr)
		}
		if n == 0 {
			break
		}
		etag, err := multipart.UploadPart(ctx, key, uploadID, partNumber, bytes.NewReader(buffer[:n]))
		if err != nil {
			return abort(err)
		}
		parts = append(parts, UploadedPart{PartNumber: partNumber, ETag: etag})
		if readErr == io.EOF || readErr == io.ErrUnexpectedEOF {
			break
		}
	}
	if err := multipart.CompleteMultipartUpload(ctx, key, uploadID, parts); err != nil {
		return abort(err)
	}
	return nil
}
EOF

export interface PatientRecord {

  strepResult: number;
  strepOutOfRange?: boolean;

  max: number;
}

/// Mix corresponding PCM samples, clipping sums to the i16 range.
pub fn mix_samples(left: &[i16], right: &[i16]) -> Vec<i16> {
    left.iter()
        .zip(right.iter())
        .map(|(&a, &b)| (i32::from(a) + i32::from(b))
            .clamp(i32::from(i16::MIN), i32::from(i16::MAX)) as i16)
        .collect()
}

    if (visited.has(start)) continue;

    const queue = [start];

from pathlib import Path

class TTLCache:
    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds):
        self.ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds
        self._items = {}

    def set(self, key, value):
        self._items[key] = (value, time.monotonic() + self.ttl_seconds)

    def get(self, key):
        entry = self._items.get(key)
        if entry is None:

export type AcuityReading = {
  site: string;
  weekEnding: string;
  visualAcuity: string;
};

export type SiteSummary = {
  site: string;
  weekEnding: string;
  normal: number;
  outOfRange: number;
};

export function summarizeWeekly(readings: AcuityReading[]): SiteSummary[] {
  const summaries = new Map<string, SiteSummary>();
  for (const reading of readings) {
    const key = JSON.stringify([reading.weekEnding, reading.site]);
    const summary = summaries.get(key) ?? {
      site: reading.site,
      weekEnding: reading.weekEnding,
      normal: 0,
      outOfRange: 0,
    };
    const match = /^20\/(\d+)$/.exec(reading.visualAcuity);
    const denominator = match ? Number(match[1]) : NaN;
    if (Number.isFinite(denominator) && denominator > 0 && denominator <= 40) {
      summary.normal += 1;
    } else {
      summary.outOfRange += 1;
    }
    summaries.set(key, summary);
  }
  return Array.from(summaries.values());
}
EOF

package emissions

import "time"

type Reading struct {
	Site    string
	Vehicle string
	Date    time.Time
	COppm   float64
}

type Counts struct {
	Normal     int
	OutOfRange int
}

func WeeklySummary(readings []Reading, weekStart time.Time) map[string]Counts {
	weekEnd := weekStart.AddDate(0, 0, 7)
	result := make(map[string]Counts)
	for _, reading := range readings {
		if reading.Date.Before(weekStart) || !reading.Date.Before(weekEnd) {
			continue
		}
		counts := result[reading.Site]
		if reading.COppm >= 0 && reading.COppm <= 9 {
			counts.Normal++
		} else {
			counts.OutOfRange++
		}
		result[reading.Site] = counts
	}
	return result
}
EOF

package pool

import "sync"

type Pool struct {
	workers int
}

func New(workers int) *Pool {
	if workers < 1 {
		workers = 1
	}
	return &Pool{workers: workers}
}

func (p *Pool) Run(jobs <-chan func()) {
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < p.workers; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for {
				job, ok := <-jobs
				if !ok {
					return
				}
				if job != nil {
					job()
				}
			}

	}

}

const fs = require('node:fs');
const readline = require('node:readline');

async function countByCountry(filePath) {
  const counts = Object.create(null);
  const input = fs.createReadStream(filePath);
  const lines = readline.createInterface({ input, crlfDelay: Infinity });
  for await (const line of lines) {
    if (line.trim() === '') continue;
    const record = JSON.parse(line);
    counts[record.country] = (counts[record.country] || 0) + 1;
  }
  return counts;
}

    .then(counts => console.log(JSON.stringify(counts, null, 2)))
    .catch(error => {

      process.exitCode = 1;
    });

class ApiClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url, opener=urlopen):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.opener = opener

cat > src/main/java/logistics/Eta.java <<'EOF'
package logistics;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public final class Eta {
    private Eta() {}

    public static List<Double> hours(List<Double> legKm, List<Double> speedKph) {
        if (legKm.size() != speedKph.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Each route leg needs one speed");
        }

        List<Double> arrivalHours = new ArrayList<>(legKm.size());
        double elapsedHours = 0.0;
        for (int i = 0; i < legKm.size(); i++) {
            double distance = legKm.get(i);
            double speed = speedKph.get(i);
            if (distance < 0.0 || speed <= 0.0) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Distances must be nonnegative and speeds positive");
            }
            elapsedHours += distance / speed;
            arrivalHours.add(elapsedHours);
        }
        return List.copyOf(arrivalHours);
    }
}
EOF

package logistics;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public final class Eta {
    private Eta() {}

    public static List<Double> hours(List<Double> legKm, List<Double> speedKph) {
        if (legKm.size() != speedKph.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Each route leg needs one speed");
        }

        List<Double> arrivalHours = new ArrayList<>(legKm.size());
        double elapsedHours = 0.0;
        for (int i = 0; i < legKm.size(); i++) {
            double distance = legKm.get(i);
            double speed = speedKph.get(i);
            if (distance < 0.0 || speed <= 0.0) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Distances must be nonnegative and speeds positive");
            }
            elapsedHours += distance / speed;
            arrivalHours.add(elapsedHours);
        }
        return List.copyOf(arrivalHours);
    }
}
EOF

use std::collections::HashMap;

pub fn parse_ini(input: &str) -> HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>> {
    let mut sections: HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut current_section: Option<String> = None;

    for line in input.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with(';') {
            continue;
        }

        if line.starts_with('[') && line.ends_with(']') {
            let name = line[1..line.len() - 1].trim().to_string();
            sections.entry(name.clone()).or_default();
            current_section = Some(name);
            continue;
        }

        if let (Some(section), Some((key, value))) =
            (current_section.as_ref(), line.split_once('='))
        {
            sections
                .entry(section.clone())
                .or_default()
                .insert(key.trim().to_string(), value.trim().to_string());
        }
    }

    sections
}
EOF
```

```bash
cat > internal/limit/bucket.go <<'EOF'
package limit

import (
	"sync"
	"time"
)

type Limiter struct {
	capacity        int
	refillPerSecond float64
	mu              sync.Mutex
	clients         map[string]bucketState
}

type bucketState struct {
	tokens   float64
	updated  time.Time
}

// New creates a limiter with the given capacity and refill rate.
func New(capacity int, refillPerSecond float64) *Limiter {
	if capacity < 0 {
		capacity = 0
	}
	if refillPerSecond < 0 {
		refillPerSecond = 0
	}
	return &Limiter{
		capacity:        capacity,
		refillPerSecond: refillPerSecond,
		clients:         make(map[string]bucketState),
	}
}

// Allow reports whether a token is available for clientID.
func (l *Limiter) Allow(clientID string) bool {
	return l.AllowAt(clientID, time.Now())
}

// AllowAt applies the bucket at now, making time-based behavior reproducible.
func (l *Limiter) AllowAt(clientID string, now time.Time) bool {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()

	if l.clients == nil {
		l.clients = make(map[string]bucketState)
	}
	state, exists := l.clients[clientID]
	if !exists {
		state = bucketState{tokens: float64(l.capacity), updated: now}
	} else if now.After(state.updated) {
		state.tokens += now.Sub(state.updated).Seconds() * l.refillPerSecond
		if state.tokens > float64(l.capacity) {
			state.tokens = float64(l.capacity)
		}
		state.updated = now
	}

	allowed := state.tokens >= 1
	if allowed {
		state.tokens--
	}
	l.clients[clientID] = state
	return allowed
}
EOF
```

/// Computes base^exponent modulo modulus.
///
/// Returns None when modulus is zero.
pub fn mod_pow(base: u64, exponent: u64, modulus: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    if modulus == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let modulus = modulus as u128;
    let mut result = 1u128 % modulus;
    let mut factor = (base as u128) % modulus;
    let mut power = exponent;
    while power != 0 {
        if power & 1 == 1 {
            result = (result * factor) % modulus;
        }
        factor = (factor * factor) % modulus;
        power >>= 1;
    }
    Some(result as u64)
}
EOF

```

```bash

cat > internal/queue/retry.go <<'EOF'
package queue

import (
	"context"
	"time"
)

type RetryPolicy struct {
	Attempts int
	Delay    time.Duration
}

func Retry(ctx context.Context, policy RetryPolicy, run func(context.Context) error) error {
	var err error
	for attempt := 0; attempt < policy.Attempts; attempt++ {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		err = run(ctx)
		if err == nil {
			return nil
		}
		timer := time.NewTimer(policy.Delay)
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			if !timer.Stop() {
				select {
				case <-timer.C:
				default:
				}
			}
			return ctx.Err()
		case <-timer.C:
		}
	}
	return err
}
EOF
d=$(mktemp -d)
sed 's/^package queue$/package main/' internal/queue/retry.go > "$d/retry.go"
cat > "$d/sample.go" <<'EOF'

	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"
)

func main() {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	calls := 0
	err := Retry(ctx, RetryPolicy{Attempts: 3, Delay: time.Millisecond}, func(context.Context) error {
		calls++
		return fmt.Errorf("retry")
	})
	fmt.Printf("%v %d\n", err, calls)
}
EOF
go run "$d/retry.go" "$d/sample.go"
rm -rf "$d"

def parse_formula(formula: str) -> dict[str, int]:
    index = 0

    def read_number() -> int:
        nonlocal index
        start = index
        while index < len(formula) and formula[index] in "0123456789":
            index += 1
        return int(formula[start:index]) if index > start else 1

    def read_group() -> dict[str, int]:
        nonlocal index
        counts: dict[str, int] = {}

                    raise ValueError("unclosed group")
                index += 1
                multiplier = read_number()
                for symbol, amount in nested.items():

            else:

                if index < len(formula) and formula[index].islower():
                    symbol += formula[index]
                    index += 1
                amount = read_number()
                counts[symbol] = counts.get(symbol, 0) + amount

                    index += 1

"""Backtracking Sudoku solver."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

Grid = list[list[int]]
FULL = sum(1 << digit for digit in range(1, 10))


def solve(grid: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> Grid:
    """Return a solved copy of a 9x9 grid."""
    if len(grid) != 9 or any(len(row) != 9 for row in grid):
        raise ValueError("grid must be 9x9")

    board = [list(row) for row in grid]
    rows = [0] * 9
    columns = [0] * 9
    boxes = [0] * 9
    empty: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    for r in range(9):
        for c in range(9):
            value = board[r][c]
            if not isinstance(value, int) or not 0 <= value <= 9:
                raise ValueError("cells must be integers from 0 to 9")
            if value == 0:
                empty.append((r, c))
                continue
            bit = 1 << value
            box = (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3
            if rows[r] & bit or columns[c] & bit or boxes[box] & bit:
                raise ValueError("grid has conflicting clues")
            rows[r] |= bit
            columns[c] |= bit
            boxes[box] |= bit

    def visit() -> bool:
        if not empty:
            return True

        best = 0
        options = 0
        fewest = 10

"""Backtracking Sudoku solver."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

Grid = list[list[int]]
FULL = sum(1 << digit for digit in range(1, 10))


def solve(grid: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> Grid:
    """Return a solved copy of a 9x9 grid."""
    if len(grid) != 9 or any(len(row) != 9 for row in grid):
        raise ValueError("grid must be 9x9")

    board = [list(row) for row in grid]
    rows = [0] * 9
    columns = [0] * 9
    boxes = [0] * 9
    empty: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    for r in range(9):
        for c in range(9):
            value = board[r][c]
            if not isinstance(value, int) or not 0 <= value <= 9:
                raise ValueError("cells must be integers from 0 to 9")
            if value == 0:
                empty.append((r, c))
                continue
            bit = 1 << value
            box = (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3
            if rows[r] & bit or columns[c] & bit or boxes[box] & bit:
                raise ValueError("grid has conflicting clues")
            rows[r] |= bit
            columns[c] |= bit
            boxes[box] |= bit

        if not empty:
            return True

        best = 0
        options = 0
        fewest = 10
        for index, (r, c) in enumerate(empty):

            available = FULL & ~(rows[r] | columns[c] | boxes[box])

            if count < fewest:
                best, options, fewest = index, available, count
                if count <= 1:

        r, c = empty.pop(best)

            bit = options & -options
            options -= bit
            value = bit.bit_length() - 1

            columns[c] |= bit
            boxes[box] |= bit

                return True
            rows[r] ^= bit
            columns[c] ^= bit
            boxes[box] ^= bit

        empty.insert(best, (r, c))
        return False

        raise ValueError("grid has no solution")

package web;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Iterator;
import java.util.Map;

public final class SessionStore {
    private final Map<String, Long> expiresAtById = new HashMap<>();

    public void put(String id, long expiresAt) {
        expiresAtById.put(id, expiresAt);
    }

    public int removeExpired(long now) {

import java.util.ArrayList;

public final class Importer {
    private Importer() {}

    public static List<PeakReading> parse(String csv) {
        List<PeakReading> readings = new ArrayList<>();
        if (csv == null || csv.isEmpty()) {
            return List.of();
        }

        String[] lines = csv.split("\\R", -1);
        for (int i = 1; i < lines.length; i++) {

            if (patientId.isEmpty()) {

                }
            } catch (NumberFormatException ignored) {
                // Ignore malformed rate values.
            }

}

package server

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

func ParsePort(raw string) (int, error) {
	text := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
	if text == "" {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("port is empty")
	}
	for _, digit := range text {
		if digit < '0' || digit > '9' {

	value, err := strconv.Atoi(text)
	if err != nil {

	if value < 1 || value > 65535 {

	}
	return value, nil
}

func parseLine(line string) (map[string]string, error) {
	fields := make(map[string]string)

		for i < len(line) && (line[i] == ' ' || line[i] == '\t' || line[i] == '\r') {
			i++

		if i == len(line) {
			break

			for i < len(line) {

				i++

					closed = true
					break

				if ch == '\\' && !escaped {
					escaped = true
				} else {
					escaped = false
				}

			}

			i++

		}

```bash
mkdir -p src && cat > src/tokenize.rs <<'EOF'
use std::io::{self, Read};

pub fn tokenize(line: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
    line.split_whitespace().collect()
}

fn quoted(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\"");
    for ch in value.chars() {
        match ch {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if c <= '\u{1f}' => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
    out
}

fn main() {
    let mut input = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input).unwrap();
    let words = tokenize(&input);
    let items = words.iter().map(|word| quoted(word)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",");
    println!("{{\"tokens\":[{}],\"count\":{}}}", items, words.len());
}
EOF
```

import json
import sys
from heapq import heappop, heappush

dependencies = json.load(sys.stdin)
targets = set(dependencies)
waiting = {target: set(names) for target, names in dependencies.items()}
unknown = {name for names in waiting.values() for name in names if name not in targets}
if unknown:
    raise SystemExit(f"unknown dependencies: {sorted(unknown)}")

ready = []
for target, names in waiting.items():
    if not names:
        heappush(ready, target)

order = []
while ready:
    emitted = heappop(ready)
    order.append(emitted)
    for target in sorted(waiting):
        if emitted in waiting[target]:
            waiting[target].remove(emitted)
            if not waiting[target]:
                heappush(ready, target)

if len(order) != len(targets):
    raise SystemExit("dependency cycle")
sys.stdout.write("\n".join(order))
if order:
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
PY

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

function parseCsvLine(line: string): string[] {
  const cells: string[] = [];
  let cell = "";
  let quoted = false;
  for (let index = 0; index < line.length; index += 1) {
    const char = line[index];
    if (quoted) {
      if (char === '"' && line[index + 1] === '"') {
        cell += '"';
        index += 1;
      } else if (char === '"') {
        quoted = false;
      } else {
        cell += char;
      }
    } else if (char === '"') {
      quoted = true;
    } else if (char === ",") {
      cells.push(cell);
      cell = "";
    } else {
      cell += char;
    }
  }
  cells.push(cell);
  return cells;
}

const inputPath = process.argv[2] ?? "data/radon.csv";
const lines = readFileSync(inputPath, "utf8").trimEnd().split(/\r?\n/);
const headers = parseCsvLine(lines[0] ?? "");
const addressIndex = headers.indexOf("address");
const concentrationIndex = headers.indexOf("radon_pCiL");
if (addressIndex < 0 || concentrationIndex < 0) {
  throw new Error("CSV must include address and radon_pCiL columns");
}

const readings = lines.slice(1).filter((line) => line.length > 0).map((line) => {
  const cells = parseCsvLine(line);
  const radon_pCiL = Number(cells[concentrationIndex]);
  if (!Number.isFinite(radon_pCiL)) {
    throw new Error("Radon concentration must be numeric");
  }
  return { address: cells[addressIndex] ?? "", radon_pCiL };
});

process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(readings));
EOF

package device;

import java.io.InputStreamReader;

import java.util.Collections;

package main

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
)

type Reading struct {
	CircuitID      string  `json:"circuit_id"`
	ResistanceMOhm float64 `json:"resistance_mohm"`
}

func importReadings(source io.Reader) ([]Reading, error) {
	reader := csv.NewReader(source)
	header, err := reader.Read()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	columns := make(map[string]int, len(header))
	for i, name := range header {
		columns[name] = i
	}
	idColumn, ok := columns["circuit_id"]
	if !ok {
		return nil, errors.New("missing circuit_id column")
	}
	valueColumn, ok := columns["resistance_mohm"]
	if !ok {
		return nil, errors.New("missing resistance_mohm column")
	}
	var readings []Reading
	for rowNumber := 2; ; rowNumber++ {
		record, err := reader.Read()
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if len(record) <= idColumn || len(record) <= valueColumn {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d has too few columns", rowNumber)
		}
		value, err := strconv.ParseFloat(record[valueColumn], 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", rowNumber, err)
		}
		readings = append(readings, Reading{
			CircuitID:      record[idColumn],
			ResistanceMOhm: math.Round(value*1000) / 1000,
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(readings, func(i, j int) bool {
		return readings[i].CircuitID < readings[j].CircuitID
	})
	return readings, nil
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: importer <csv>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	file, err := os.Open(os.Args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer file.Close()
	readings, err := importReadings(file)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if err := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(readings); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
EOF

import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

type Position = {
  board: string[][];
  row: number;
  col: number;
  player: string;
};

const { board, row, col, player } = JSON.parse(
  readFileSync("data/position.json", "utf8"),
) as Position;

const directions: Array<[number, number]> = [
  [0, 1],
  [1, 0],
  [1, 1],
  [1, -1],
];

function hasFour(): boolean {
  for (const [dr, dc] of directions) {
    let count = 1;
    for (const sign of [-1, 1]) {
      let r = row + sign * dr;
      let c = col + sign * dc;
      while (
        r >= 0 &&
        r < board.length &&
        c >= 0 &&
        c < board[r].length &&
        board[r][c] === player
      ) {
        count++;
        r += sign * dr;
        c += sign * dc;
      }
    }
    if (count >= 4) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

mkdirSync("out", { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(
  "out/win.json",
  JSON.stringify({ wins: hasFour() }) + "\n",
  { encoding: "utf8" },
);
EOF

use std::{env, process};

fn mod_pow(base: u64, mut exponent: u64, modulus: u64) -> Result<u64, &'static str> {
    if modulus == 0 {
        return Err("modulus must be positive");
    }
    let m = modulus as u128;
    let mut factor = (base % modulus) as u128;
    let mut result = 1u128 % m;
    while exponent > 0 {
        if exponent & 1 == 1 {
            result = result * factor % m;
        }
        factor = factor * factor % m;
        exponent >>= 1;
    }
    Ok(result as u64)
}

fn main() {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().skip(1).collect();
    if args.len() != 3 {
        eprintln!("usage: modpow BASE EXPONENT MODULUS");
        process::exit(2);
    }
    let numbers: Vec<u64> = args.iter().map(|value| {
        value.parse::<u64>().unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            eprintln!("arguments must be unsigned integers");
            process::exit(2);

    let (base, exponent, modulus) = (numbers[0], numbers[1], numbers[2]);
    let result = mod_pow(base, exponent, modulus).unwrap_or_else(|message| {
        eprintln!("{message}");
        process::exit(2);
    });
    println!("{{\"base\":{},\"exponent\":{},\"modulus\":{},\"result\":{}}}",
             base, exponent, modulus, result);
}

package zones

import "math"

type Point struct {
	X float64 `json:"x"`
	Y float64 `json:"y"`
}

const epsilon = 1e-9

func onSegment(p, a, b Point) bool {
	cross := (p.X-a.X)*(b.Y-a.Y) - (p.Y-a.Y)*(b.X-a.X)
	if math.Abs(cross) > epsilon {
		return false
	}
	return p.X >= math.Min(a.X, b.X)-epsilon && p.X <= math.Max(a.X, b.X)+epsilon &&
		p.Y >= math.Min(a.Y, b.Y)-epsilon && p.Y <= math.Max(a.Y, b.Y)+epsilon
}

func Contains(point Point, polygon []Point) bool {
	if len(polygon) < 3 {
		return false
	}
	inside := false
	for i, j := 0, len(polygon)-1; i < len(polygon); j, i = i, i+1 {
		a, b := polygon[j], polygon[i]
		if onSegment(point, a, b) {
			return true
		}
		if (a.Y > point.Y) != (b.Y > point.Y) {
			x := (b.X-a.X)*(point.Y-a.Y)/(b.Y-a.Y) + a.X
			if point.X < x {
				inside = !inside
			}
		}
	}
	return inside
}
EOF

package main

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

type siteSummary struct {
	Site            string `json:"site"`
	NormalCount     int    `json:"normal_count"`
	OutOfRangeCount int    `json:"out_of_range_count"`
}
type weeklyReport struct {
	Sites []siteSummary `json:"sites"`
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func run() error {
	input, err := os.Open("data/readings.csv")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer input.Close()
	rows, err := csv.NewReader(input).ReadAll()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("readings file has no header")
	}
	counts := make(map[string]*siteSummary)
	for line, row := range rows[1:] {
		if len(row) != 2 {
			return fmt.Errorf("row %d must have two columns", line+2)
		}
		site := strings.TrimSpace(row[0])
		value, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(row[1]), 64)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", line+2, err)
		}
		item := counts[site]
		if item == nil {
			item = &siteSummary{Site: site}
			counts[site] = item
		}
		if value >= 1.0 {
			item.NormalCount++
		} else {
			item.OutOfRangeCount++
		}
	}
	names := make([]string, 0, len(counts))
	for site := range counts {
		names = append(names, site)
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	result := weeklyReport{Sites: make([]siteSummary, 0, len(names))}
	for _, site := range names {
		result.Sites = append(result.Sites, *counts[site])
	}
	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(result, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll("reports", 0755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile("reports/weekly_summary.json", append(data, '\n'), 0644)
}
EOF

import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

counts = {}
with Path("data/readings.csv").open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as source:
    for row in csv.DictReader(source):
        site = row["site"]
        item = counts.setdefault(site, {
            "site": site, "normal_count": 0, "out_of_range_count": 0
        })
        field = "normal_count" if float(row["megohms"]) >= 1.0 else "out_of_range_count"
        item[field] += 1

document = json.loads(Path("reports/weekly_summary.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
sites = document.get("sites") if isinstance(document, dict) else None
computed = sorted(counts.values(), key=lambda item: item["site"])
if sites != computed:
    raise SystemExit("summary values do not match the readings")
print("summary JSON is valid for the readings")

cat > internal/electrical/weekly_summary.go <<'EOF'
package main

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

type siteSummary struct {
	Site            string `json:"site"`
	NormalCount     int    `json:"normal_count"`
	OutOfRangeCount int    `json:"out_of_range_count"`
}
type weeklyReport struct {
	Sites []siteSummary `json:"sites"`
}

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func run() error {
	input, err := os.Open("data/readings.csv")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer input.Close()
	rows, err := csv.NewReader(input).ReadAll()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("readings file has no header")
	}
	counts := make(map[string]*siteSummary)
	for line, row := range rows[1:] {
		if len(row) != 2 {
			return fmt.Errorf("row %d must have two columns", line+2)
		}
		site := strings.TrimSpace(row[0])
		value, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(row[1]), 64)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", line+2, err)
		}
		item := counts[site]
		if item == nil {
			item = &siteSummary{Site: site}
			counts[site] = item
		}
		if value >= 1.0 {
			item.NormalCount++
		} else {
			item.OutOfRangeCount++
		}
	}
	names := make([]string, 0, len(counts))
	for site := range counts {
		names = append(names, site)
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	result := weeklyReport{Sites: make([]siteSummary, 0, len(names))}
	for _, site := range names {
		result.Sites = append(result.Sites, *counts[site])
	}
	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(result, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll("reports", 0755); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile("reports/weekly_summary.json", append(data, '\n'), 0644)
}
EOF
go run internal/electrical/weekly_summary.go && cat reports/weekly_summary.json
```

import json
import sys

rows = ["09:15-17:45 lunch 30m", "08:40-12:10 lunch 0m"]

def minutes(line):
    span, _, pause = line.partition(" lunch ")
    start, end = span.split("-")
    sh, sm = map(int, start.split(":"))
    eh, em = map(int, end.split(":"))
    return eh * 60 + em - sh * 60 - sm - int(pause[:-1])

values = [minutes(row) for row in rows]
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
if set(data) != {"entries", "total_minutes"}:
    raise SystemExit("invalid output fields")
if data["entries"] != values or data["total_minutes"] != sum(values):
    raise SystemExit("invalid output values")

import json
import re
import sys


def worked_minutes(line):
    match = re.fullmatch(
        r"\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})-(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s+lunch\s+(\d+)m\s*",
        line,
    )
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid timesheet entry: {line!r}")
    sh, sm, eh, em, lunch = map(int, match.groups())
    return eh * 60 + em - sh * 60 - sm - lunch


entries = [worked_minutes(line) for line in sys.stdin if line.strip()]
print(json.dumps({"entries": entries, "total_minutes": sum(entries)}))
PY

stats = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])

import csv
import json
from collections import defaultdict

stats = defaultdict(lambda: {"points": 0, "goal_difference": 0})
with open("league/results.csv", newline="") as source:
    for row in csv.DictReader(source):
        home, away = row["home"], row["away"]
        home_goals = int(row["home_goals"])
        away_goals = int(row["away_goals"])

            stats[home]["points"] += 3
        elif home_goals < away_goals:
            stats[away]["points"] += 3
        else:
            stats[home]["points"] += 1
            stats[away]["points"] += 1

standings = [{"team": team, **values} for team, values in stats.items()]
standings.sort(key=lambda row: (-row["points"], -row["goal_difference"], row["team"]))
print(json.dumps({"league": "North Coast Cup", "standings": standings}))

import argparse
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path


def read_readings(source: Path) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    with source.open("r", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        rows = csv.DictReader(handle)
        return [
            {
                "employee_id": row["employee_id"],
                "recorded_at": row["recorded_at"],
                "reading_type": row["reading_type"],
                "value": float(row["value"]),
            }
            for row in rows
        ]


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("csv_path", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    readings = read_readings(args.csv_path)
    destination = Path("reports/screen_readings.json")
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with destination.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(readings, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        handle.write("\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import heapq
import json
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from typing import Any


def top_orders(orders: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    largest = heapq.nlargest(10, orders, key=lambda order: float(order["total"]))
    return [
        {"order_id": order["order_id"], "total": round(float(order["total"]), 2)}
        for order in largest
    ]


def main() -> None:
    with open("orders.json", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        orders = json.load(source)
    print(json.dumps(top_orders(orders)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

package main

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
)

type Summary struct {
	Site string `json:"site"`
	NormalCount int `json:"normal_count"`
	OutOfRangeCount int `json:"out_of_range_count"`
}

func main() {
	r := csv.NewReader(os.Stdin)
	header, err := r.Read()
	if err != nil { fail(err) }

	for site := range counts { sites = append(sites, site) }
	sort.Strings(sites)
	out := make([]Summary, 0, len(sites))
	for _, site := range sites { out = append(out, *counts[site]) }
	fail(json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(out))
}

	if err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err); os.Exit(1) }
}

import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime

def parse(value):
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00"))

def stamp(value):
    return value.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")

def merge(intervals):
    ordered = sorted((parse(start), parse(end)) for start, end in intervals)
    merged = []
    for start, end in ordered:
        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])
    return merged

data = json.load(sys.stdin)
day_start, day_end = parse(data["day_start"]), parse(data["day_end"])
busy = merge(data["busy_intervals"])
free = []
cursor = day_start
for start, end in busy:
    if cursor < start:
        free.append([cursor, start])
    cursor = max(cursor, end)
if cursor < day_end:
    free.append([cursor, day_end])
result = {"busy": [[stamp(a), stamp(b)] for a, b in busy],
          "free": [[stamp(a), stamp(b)] for a, b in free]}
json.dump(result, sys.stdout, separators=(",", ":"))
sys.stdout.write("\n")
PY

def encode_row(row: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    runs: list[list[int]] = []

            runs[-1][1] += 1
        else:

from collections import defaultdict

import json
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    totals = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])

            "out_of_range_count": outside,
        })
    destination = Path("out/weekly_summary.json")
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    destination.write_text(

    )

```bash
mkdir -p scripts
cat > scripts/pg_dump_all.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
mkdir -p backups
database_list=$(psql -At -c 'SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate = false AND datallowconn = true ORDER BY datname COLLATE "C";')
while IFS= read -r database; do
  [[ -z "$database" ]] && continue
  pg_dump --dbname="$database" | gzip -c > "backups/${database}.sql.gz"

```bash
cat > src/main/java/roadside/WeeklySummary.java <<'EOF'
package roadside;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

public class WeeklySummary {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Map<String, int[]> counts = new TreeMap<>();
        List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(Path.of("data/weekly.csv"));
        for (int i = 1; i < lines.size(); i++) {
            String[] fields = lines.get(i).split(",", -1);
            String site = fields[0];
            double bac = Double.parseDouble(fields[1]);
            int[] siteCounts = counts.computeIfAbsent(site, key -> new int[2]);
            siteCounts[bac <= 0.08 ? 0 : 1]++;
        }

        StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder("[");
        boolean first = true;
        for (Map.Entry<String, int[]> entry : counts.entrySet()) {
            if (!first) output.append(',');
            first = false;
            int[] values = entry.getValue();
            output.append("{\"site\":").append(jsonString(entry.getKey()))
                  .append(",\"normal\":").append(values[0])
                  .append(",\"out_of_range\":").append(values[1]).append('}');
        }
        System.out.println(output.append(']'));
    }

    private static String jsonString(String value) {
        return "\"" + value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"";
    }
}
EOF

package roadside;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

public class WeeklySummary {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Map<String, int[]> counts = new TreeMap<>();
        List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(Path.of("data/weekly.csv"));
        for (int i = 1; i < lines.size(); i++) {
            String[] fields = lines.get(i).split(",", -1);
            String site = fields[0];
            double bac = Double.parseDouble(fields[1]);
            int[] siteCounts = counts.computeIfAbsent(site, key -> new int[2]);
            siteCounts[bac <= 0.08 ? 0 : 1]++;
        }

        StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder("[");
        boolean first = true;
        for (Map.Entry<String, int[]> entry : counts.entrySet()) {
            if (!first) output.append(',');
            first = false;
            int[] values = entry.getValue();
            output.append("{\"site\":").append(jsonString(entry.getKey()))
                  .append(",\"normal\":").append(values[0])
                  .append(",\"out_of_range\":").append(values[1]).append('}');
        }
        System.out.println(output.append(']'));
    }

    private static String jsonString(String value) {
        return "\"" + value.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"";
    }
}
EOF

};

func ValidateFile(path string) (int, int, error) {
	file, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, err

	}
	return valid, invalid, nil
}

I’ll implement the bounded C formatter and write its UTF-8 result to the required path.
```bash
mkdir -p src data out
cat > src/status.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stddef.h>

int main(void) {
    char node[48];
    unsigned int code;
    FILE *input = fopen("data/reading.txt", "r");
    if (input == NULL) return 1;
    int fields = fscanf(input, "%47s %u", node, &code);
    if (fclose(input) != 0 || fields != 2) return 1;

    char message[80];
    int length = snprintf(message, sizeof message,
                          "node=%s;code=%u\n", node, code);
    if (length < 0 || (size_t)length >= sizeof message) return 1;

    FILE *output = fopen("out/status.txt", "w");
    if (output == NULL) return 1;
    int written = fwrite(message, 1, (size_t)length, output) == (size_t)length;
    if (fclose(output) != 0) written = 0;
    return written ? 0 : 1;
}
EOF
printf 'cedar 27\n' > data/reading.txt
gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror src/status.c -o /tmp/status_writer &&
/tmp/status_writer &&
cat out/status.txt

package ledger;

import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.util.Scanner;

public final class MathUtil {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        BigInteger gcd = BigInteger.ZERO;
        int count = 0;
        try (Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in)) {
            while (scanner.hasNext()) {
                BigInteger value = new BigInteger(scanner.next());
                gcd = gcd.gcd(value);
                count++;
            }
        }
        System.out.printf("{\"gcd\":%s,\"count\":%d}%n", gcd, count);
    }
}
EOF

```bash
mkdir -p src/hvac && cat > src/hvac/weeklySummary.js <<'EOF'
const fs = require("fs");

const rows = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("data/weekly_readings.json", "utf8"));
const totals = new Map();

for (const row of rows) {
  if (!totals.has(row.site)) {
    totals.set(row.site, {
      site: row.site,
      normal_count: 0,
      out_of_range_count: 0,
    });
  }
  const total = totals.get(row.site);
  for (const value of row.readings) {
    if (value >= 0 && value <= 5) total.normal_count += 1;
    else total.out_of_range_count += 1;
  }
}

const sites = [...totals.values()].sort((a, b) =>
  a.site < b.site ? -1 : a.site > b.site ? 1 : 0
);
process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ sites })}\n`);
EOF

I’ll implement recursive nonblank-line counting and emit the required JSON object.
```bash
cat > src/loc.rs <<'EOF'
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fmt::Write as _;
use std::io;
use std::path::Path;

fn visit(dir: &Path, counts: &mut BTreeMap<String, usize>) -> io::Result<()> {
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
        let path = entry?.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            visit(&path, counts)?;
        } else if path.is_file() {
            let ext = path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("(none)").to_owned();
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)?;
            let lines = text.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()).count();
            *counts.entry(ext).or_default() += lines;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn quoted(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\"");
    for ch in value.chars() {
        match ch {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if c <= '\u{1f}' => write!(&mut out, "\\u{:04x}", c as u32).unwrap(),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
    out
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root = std::env::args().nth(1).ok_or_else(|| {
        io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "usage: loc <directory>")
    })?;
    let mut counts = BTreeMap::new();
    visit(Path::new(&root), &mut counts)?;
    print!("{{");
    for (index, (extension, count)) in counts.iter().enumerate() {
        if index > 0 {
            print!(",");
        }
        print!("{}:{}", quoted(extension), count);
    }
    println!("}}");
    Ok(())
}
EOF
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash

dir=${1:?usage: lower.sh DIRECTORY}

const fs = require('fs');

const inputPath = process.argv[2] || 'data/partner_readings.csv';
const text = fs.readFileSync(inputPath, 'utf8').trim();
const [headerLine, ...lines] = text.split(/\r?\n/);
const headers = headerLine.split(',');
const idIndex = headers.indexOf('circuit_id');
const startIndex = headers.indexOf('pressure_start_kpa');
const endIndex = headers.indexOf('pressure_end_kpa');

if ([idIndex, startIndex, endIndex].some(index => index < 0)) {
  throw new Error('CSV is missing a required column.');
}

const records = lines.filter(Boolean).map(line => {
  const cells = line.split(',');
  const drop = Number(cells[startIndex]) - Number(cells[endIndex]);
  return {
    circuit_id: cells[idIndex],
    pressure_drop_kpa: Math.round((drop + Number.EPSILON) * 100) / 100,
  };
});

records.sort((a, b) => a.circuit_id.localeCompare(b.circuit_id));
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(records) + '\n');
EOF
