#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct {
    int64_t timestamp;
    unsigned sensor_id;
} SensorRecord;

/* Sort by timestamp, then sensor ID; works for every array length. */
static int compare_records(const void *left, const void *right) {
    const SensorRecord *a = left, *b = right;
    if (a->timestamp != b->timestamp)
        return (a->timestamp > b->timestamp) - (a->timestamp < b->timestamp);
    return (a->sensor_id > b->sensor_id) - (a->sensor_id < b->sensor_id);
}

static void sort_records(SensorRecord *records, size_t count) {
    if (count > 1)
        qsort(records, count, sizeof *records, compare_records);
}

int main(void) {

    size_t count = sizeof records / sizeof records[0];
    sort_records(records, count);

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct {
    int64_t timestamp;
    unsigned sensor_id;
} SensorRecord;

/* Sort by timestamp, then sensor ID; works for every array length. */
static int comes_after(SensorRecord a, SensorRecord b) {
    return a.timestamp > b.timestamp ||
           (a.timestamp == b.timestamp && a.sensor_id > b.sensor_id);
}

static void sort_records(SensorRecord *records, size_t count) {
    for (size_t i = 1; i < count; ++i) {
        SensorRecord value = records[i];
        size_t j = i;
        while (j && comes_after(records[j - 1], value)) {
            records[j] = records[j - 1];
            --j;
        }
        records[j] = value;
    }
}

    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        printf("%lld:%u\n", (long long)records[i].timestamp, records[i].sensor_id);

def _render(value, depth=0):
    pad = '  ' * depth
    if isinstance(value, dict):

            return '{}'
        rows = ('  ' * (depth + 1) + _quote(key) + ': ' + _render(item, depth + 1)

    if value is None:

    if value is True:

/** Serialize a valid Date as UTC ISO 8601 with millisecond precision. */
export function serializeDate(date: Date): string {
  const pad = (n: number, width = 2) => String(n).padStart(width, "0");
  const year = date.getUTCFullYear();
  const yearText = year < 0 || year > 9999

    : pad(year, 4);
  return `${yearText}-${pad(date.getUTCMonth() + 1)}-${pad(date.getUTCDate())}T${pad(date.getUTCHours())}:${pad(date.getUTCMinutes())}:${pad(date.getUTCSeconds())}.${pad(date.getUTCMilliseconds(), 3)}Z`;
}
EOF

def copy_template(source: Path, destination: Path) -> None:

from math import gcd

def _parse(text: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Parse signed rational text without approximate numeric values."""
    a, slash, b = text.partition("/")
    return int(a), int(b) if slash else 1

def _format(n: int, d: int) -> str:
    """Render a reduced rational string, omitting a denominator of one."""
    divisor = gcd(abs(n), d)
    n, d = n // divisor, d // divisor
    return str(n) if d == 1 else f"{n}/{d}"

def scale_quantities(quantities: list[str], factor: str) -> list[str]:
    """Scale signed rational recipe amounts with exact rational arithmetic."""
    fn, fd = _parse(factor)
    return [_format(n * fn, d * fd) for n, d in map(_parse, quantities)]
EOF

				return false
			}
			value = value*10 + int(c-'0')
			if value > 255 {
				return false
			}
		}
	}
	return true
}

import re


def render(message: str, values: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """Render a notification with Python Template marker rules.

    Recognize valid $name and ${name} forms, convert $$ to one dollar, and
    retain absent names and malformed markers. Values are strings supplied
    by the caller; no conversion or mutation of the mapping is needed.

    def replace(match):
        token = match.group(1)
        if token in ("", "$):
            return "$"
        key = token[1:-1] if token.startswith("{") else token

    return re.sub(pattern, replace, message)
EOF

Keep duplicates; order by item_id and separate names with comma-space.
The source guarantees non-null names and unique item_id values per order.

WITH RECURSIVE ranked AS (
 SELECT order_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY item_id) AS n,

 FROM order_items

)
SELECT order_id, names AS product_names FROM walk WHERE n=total ORDER BY order_id;
EOF

#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

struct SensorRecord { int64_t timestamp; int sensor_id; };

/* Order records by signed timestamp; ties may appear in any order. */
static int compare_timestamp(const void *left, const void *right) {
    const struct SensorRecord *a = left, *b = right;
    return (a->timestamp > b->timestamp) - (a->timestamp < b->timestamp);
}

void order_records(struct SensorRecord *records, size_t count) {
    if (count > 1) qsort(records, count, sizeof *records, compare_timestamp);
}

int main(void) {
    struct SensorRecord records[] = {{42, 7}, {-3, 2}, {18, 9}, {0, 4}};
    order_records(records, sizeof records / sizeof records[0]);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof records / sizeof records[0]; ++i)
        printf("%" PRId64 ":%d\n", records[i].timestamp, records[i].sensor_id);
    return 0;
}
EOF
```

#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

struct SensorRecord { int64_t timestamp; int sensor_id; };

/* Order records by signed timestamp; ties may appear in any order. */
static int compare_timestamp(const void *left, const void *right) {
    const struct SensorRecord *a = left, *b = right;
    return (a->timestamp > b->timestamp) - (a->timestamp < b->timestamp);
}

void order_records(struct SensorRecord *records, size_t count) {
    if (count > 1) for (size_t i = 1; i < count; ++i) {
        struct SensorRecord item = records[i]; size_t j = i;
        while (j > 0 && compare_timestamp(&records[j - 1], &item) > 0) {
            records[j] = records[j - 1]; --j;
        }
        records[j] = item;
    }
}

int main(void) {
    struct SensorRecord records[] = {{42, 7}, {-3, 2}, {18, 9}, {0, 4}};
    order_records(records, sizeof records / sizeof records[0]);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof records / sizeof records[0]; ++i)
        printf("%" PRId64 ":%d\n", records[i].timestamp, records[i].sensor_id);

import re
from pathlib import Path

_FIELD = re.compile(r'(?:^|,)(?:"((?:[^"]|"")*)"|([^,]*))')


def _row(line: str) -> list[str]:
    return [
        quoted.replace('""', '"') if quoted else plain
        for quoted, plain in _FIELD.findall(line)
    ]


def read_transactions(path: str | Path) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Read an exported UTF-8 transaction file as dictionaries of string values.

    Input uses a unique, nonempty header and valid comma-delimited CSV fields.
    Fields may be double-quoted; embedded quote characters are doubled. Records
    use LF separators, contain no embedded line breaks or blank rows, and have
    exactly one field per header. Preserve header spelling, empty fields,
    whitespace, and parsed text; do not coerce dates or amounts to other types.
    """
    lines = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n")
    if lines[-1] == "":
        lines.pop()
    header = _row(lines[0])
    return [dict(zip(header, _row(line))) for line in lines[1:]]
EOF

func ParseCallback(raw string) (host, path string, err error) {
	i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
	if i < 0 || (raw[:i] != "http" && raw[:i] != "https") { return "", "", errors.New("callback must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL") }

	if strings.HasPrefix(rest, "/") {
		if j = strings.IndexAny(rest, "?#"); j >= 0 { rest = rest[:j] }

	}

def parse_command(text: str) -> list[str]:

I'll write the matching manual formatter with a byte-copy loop and reversed decimal digits. Its append routine observes the capacity rule, while the final length determines whether the full message fits. Keeping the field sequence in one place makes the output layout clear to maintain.
```bash

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <limits.h>

/* Format an ASCII state label and unsigned code in a bounded buffer. */
static void emit(char *d, size_t c, size_t *n, char x) { if (*n + 1 < c) d[*n] = x; ++*n; }
bool format_status(char *dst, size_t cap, const char *state, unsigned int code) {
    if (!cap) return false;
    size_t n = 0;
    const char *parts[] = {"state=", state, " code="};
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 3; ++i)
        for (const char *p = parts[i]; *p; ++p) emit(dst, cap, &n, *p);
    char digits[sizeof code * CHAR_BIT]; size_t m = 0;
    do { digits[m++] = (char)('0' + code % 10); code /= 10; } while (code);
    while (m) emit(dst, cap, &n, digits[--m]);
    dst[n < cap ? n : cap - 1] = '\0';
    return n < cap;
}
EOF

    """Return whether a valid client belongs to any valid IPv4/IPv6 CIDR.
    Treat subnet host bits as network bits; an empty iterable returns False."""
    version = 6 if ":" in client else 4
    family, width = (socket.AF_INET6, 128) if version == 6 else (socket.AF_INET, 32)
    address = int.from_bytes(socket.inet_pton(family, client), "big")

        bits = int(prefix[0]) if prefix else width
        network = int.from_bytes(socket.inet_pton(family, host), "big")
        mask = ((1 << bits) - 1) << (width - bits) if bits else 0

def _u32le(raw: bytes) -> int:
    return raw[0] | (raw[1] << 8) | (raw[2] << 16) | (raw[3] << 24)

def parse_header(data: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, int, int]:

    if len(data) != 12:

    magic = data[:4]

from collections.abc import Sequence

def common_parent(paths: Sequence[str]) -> str:
    """Return the shared directory prefix for canonical absolute POSIX paths.

    The sequence is nonempty; paths are canonical absolute POSIX paths.
    """
    parts = [path.split('/')[1:] for path in paths]
    shared = []
    for group in zip(*parts):
        if len(set(group)) != 1:

        shared.append(group[0])
    return '/' + '/'.join(shared)

    Blank strings map to unassigned; all other strings reach the region index.

    normalized = postcode.strip().upper()
    if not normalized:
        return "unassigned"
    for prefix, zone in _ZONE_RULES:
        if normalized[0] == prefix:

    return "central"

from pathlib import Path

def find_matches(root: str, pattern: str = "*.log") -> list[str]:
    """Return sorted relative POSIX paths for a case-sensitive filename glob."""
    base = Path(root).resolve()
    paths = base.rglob(pattern, case_sensitive=True)

    base = Path(root).resolve()

import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
from threading import Lock, Thread
from urllib.request import urlopen

def download(urls, output_dir):
    """Save each reachable thumbnail URL as an indexed binary file."""
    output = Path(output_dir); output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    results = [None] * len(urls); items = iter(enumerate(urls)); lock = Lock()
    def worker():

            if item is None: return
            index, url = item

    for thread in threads: thread.start()
    for thread in threads: thread.join()

package users

import "unicode"

// MatchName reports whether two valid UTF-8 account usernames match using
// Go's Unicode simple case-fold rules. It performs no locale-specific
// conversion or normalization; fold-equivalent rune sequences match.
func MatchName(a, b string) bool {
	left, right := []rune(a), []rune(b)
	if len(left) != len(right) {
		return false
	}

			r = unicode.SimpleFold(r)
			if r == left[i] {
				return false
			}
		}
	}
	return true
}
EOF

def parse_cookie_header(header: str | None) -> dict[str, str]:

import os


def retry_delay(attempt: int, base_delay: float | None = None, cap: float = 60.0) -> float:
    """Return the capped exponential delay before a retry; attempts are one-based."""
    if attempt < 1:
        raise ValueError("attempt must be positive")
    if base_delay is None:

from collections.abc import Sequence


def best_trade(prices: Sequence[float]) -> tuple[int, int, float] | None:
    if len(prices) < 2:
        return None

    lowest_price = prices[0]
    lowest_day = 0
    best: tuple[int, int, float] | None = None

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

_PART_SIZE = int(os.environ.get("UPLOAD_PART_SIZE", "0"))


@dataclass
class UploadProgress:
    total_bytes: int
    received_ranges: list[tuple[int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)

    def add_range(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Record a received half-open byte interval [start, end)."""
        if start < 0 or end < start or end > self.total_bytes:
            raise ValueError("range is outside the upload")
        if start == end:
            return

        merged: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        for left, right in sorted(self.received_ranges + [(start, end)]):
            if merged and left <= merged[-1][1]:
                old_left, old_right = merged[-1]
                merged[-1] = (old_left, max(old_right, right))
            else:
                merged.append((left, right))
        self.received_ranges = merged

    def missing_ranges(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        """Return uncovered intervals, divided by the configured part size."""
        gaps: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        cursor = 0
        for start, end in self.received_ranges:
            if cursor < start:
                gaps.extend(self._split_gap(cursor, start))
            cursor = max(cursor, end)
        if cursor < self.total_bytes:
            gaps.extend(self._split_gap(cursor, self.total_bytes))
        return gaps

    @staticmethod
    def _split_gap(start: int, end: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        if _PART_SIZE <= 0:
            return [(start, end)]
        result: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        while start < end:
            boundary = (start // _PART_SIZE + 1) * _PART_SIZE
            next_end = min(end, boundary)
            result.append((start, next_end))
            start = next_end
        return result
PY

import csv

def import_germination_readings(source):

        if not 0 <= germination_pct <= 100:
            raise ValueError("Germination must be between 0 and 100")

            "tested_on": tested_on,

    let rows = grid.len();

        return Vec::new();
    }
    let cols = grid[0].len();
    if cols == 0 {
        return vec![Vec::new(); rows];
    }
    let mut next = vec![vec![false; cols]; rows];

                }
            }
            next[r][c] = if grid[r][c] {
                neighbors == 2 || neighbors == 3
            } else {
                neighbors == 3
            };

    }
    next
}'''

from datetime import date

NORMAL_INTERVAL = (35.0, 37.5)

def weekly_summary(rows):
    grouped = {}
    for row in rows:
        site = row["site"]
        day = date.fromisoformat(row["date"])
        year, week, _ = day.isocalendar()
        key = (site, year, week)
        counts = grouped.setdefault(key, {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})

        if lower <= float(row["value"]) <= upper:

        else:
            counts["out_of_range"] += 1

def longest_palindrome(text: str) -> str:
    """Return the earliest longest palindromic substring."""
    if not text:

    for center in range(len(text)):

Implement a CSV importer in `src/hvac/importer.js` for partner refrigerant circuit pressure-decay readings. Return circuit ID, timestamp, and pressure in psi, and reject malformed rows.

<think>I’ll parse the partner’s columns, validate each reading, and use the configured pressure unit for conversion, with a clear default when no setting is present.</think>
I’m implementing the importer with row validation and configured unit conversion.
```bash
cat > src/hvac/importer.js <<'EOF'
const KPA_TO_PSI = 0.1450377377;

function importPressureDecayCsv(csv) {
  const lines = csv.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
  if (!lines[0]) return [];

  const headers = lines[0].split(',').map((header) => header.trim());
  const required = ['circuit_id', 'recorded_at', 'pressure'];
  for (const name of required) {
    if (!headers.includes(name)) throw new Error(`Missing column: ${name}`);
  }

  const unit = process.env.HVAC_PARTNER_PRESSURE_UNIT || 'psi';
  if (unit !== 'psi' && unit !== 'kPa') throw new Error(`Unsupported pressure unit: ${unit}`);

  return lines.slice(1).filter((line) => line.trim()).map((line, index) => {
    const cells = line.split(',');
    const row = Object.fromEntries(headers.map((name, column) => [name, (cells[column] || '').trim()]));
    const pressure = Number(row.pressure);
    if (!row.circuit_id || !row.recorded_at || row.pressure === '' || !Number.isFinite(pressure)) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid pressure reading on row ${index + 2}`);
    }
    return {
      circuitId: row.circuit_id,
      recordedAt: row.recorded_at,
      pressurePsi: unit === 'kPa' ? pressure * KPA_TO_PSI : pressure,
    };
  });
}

module.exports = { importPressureDecayCsv };
EOF

from __future__ import annotations

Grid = list[list[int]]


def solve(grid: Grid) -> Grid | None:
    """Solve a 9x9 Sudoku by backtracking, returning None if unsolvable."""
    if len(grid) != 9 or any(not isinstance(row, list) or len(row) != 9 for row in grid):
        return None
    board = [row[:] for row in grid]

    def allowed(row: int, col: int, value: int) -> bool:
        if any(board[row][i] == value or board[i][col] == value for i in range(9)):
            return False
        box_row, box_col = (row // 3) * 3, (col // 3) * 3
        return all(
            board[r][c] != value
            for r in range(box_row, box_row + 3)
            for c in range(box_col, box_col + 3)
        )

    for row in range(9):
        for col in range(9):
            value = board[row][col]
            if not isinstance(value, int) or not 0 <= value <= 9:
                return None
            if value:
                board[row][col] = 0
                valid = allowed(row, col, value)
                board[row][col] = value
                if not valid:
                    return None

    def search() -> bool:
        for row in range(9):
            for col in range(9):
                if board[row][col] == 0:
                    for value in range(1, 10):
                        if allowed(row, col, value):
                            board[row][col] = value
                            if search():
                                return True
                            board[row][col] = 0
                    return False
        return True

    return board if search() else None
PY

```bash

cat > src/symtab.c <<'EOF'
#include "symtab.h"
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct Entry {
    char *name;
    int value;
    struct Entry *next;
} Entry;

struct Symtab {
    Entry **buckets;
    size_t capacity;
    size_t size;
};

static uint64_t hash_name(const char *name) {
    uint64_t hash = 5381;
    for (; *name; ++name) hash = hash * 33u ^ (unsigned char)*name;
    return hash;
}

static int resize_table(Symtab *table) {
    size_t capacity = table->capacity * 2;
    Entry **buckets = calloc(capacity, sizeof(*buckets));
    if (!buckets) return 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < table->capacity; ++i) {
        Entry *entry = table->buckets[i];
        while (entry) {
            Entry *next = entry->next;
            size_t index = hash_name(entry->name) % capacity;
            entry->next = buckets[index];
            buckets[index] = entry;
            entry = next;
        }
    }
    free(table->buckets);
    table->buckets = buckets;
    table->capacity = capacity;
    return 1;
}

Symtab *symtab_create(void) {
    Symtab *table = calloc(1, sizeof(*table));
    if (!table) return NULL;
    table->capacity = 8;
    table->buckets = calloc(table->capacity, sizeof(*table->buckets));
    if (!table->buckets) { free(table); return NULL; }
    return table;
}

void symtab_destroy(Symtab *table) {
    if (!table) return;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < table->capacity; ++i) {
        Entry *entry = table->buckets[i];
        while (entry) {
            Entry *next = entry->next;
            free(entry->name);
            free(entry);
            entry = next;
        }
    }
    free(table->buckets);
    free(table);
}

int symtab_insert(Symtab *table, const char *name, int value) {
    if (!table || !name) return 0;
    size_t index = hash_name(name) % table->capacity;
    for (Entry *entry = table->buckets[index]; entry; entry = entry->next) {
        if (strcmp(entry->name, name) == 0) { entry->value = value; return 1; }
    }
    if ((table->size + 1) * 5 > table->capacity * 4) {
        if (!resize_table(table)) return 0;
        index = hash_name(name) % table->capacity;
    }
    Entry *entry = malloc(sizeof(*entry));
    if (!entry) return 0;
    size_t length = strlen(name) + 1;
    entry->name = malloc(length);
    if (!entry->name) { free(entry); return 0; }
    memcpy(entry->name, name, length);
    entry->value = value;
    entry->next = table->buckets[index];
    table->buckets[index] = entry;
    ++table->size;
    return 1;
}

int symtab_lookup(const Symtab *table, const char *name, int *value) {
    if (!table || !name || !value) return 0;
    size_t index = hash_name(name) % table->capacity;
    for (Entry *entry = table->buckets[index]; entry; entry = entry->next) {
        if (strcmp(entry->name, name) == 0) { *value = entry->value; return 1; }
    }
    return 0;
}

size_t symtab_bucket_count(const Symtab *table) {
    return table ? table->capacity : 0;
}
EOF

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
)

type fileRecord struct {
	path string
	size int64
}

func largestFiles(root string) ([]fileRecord, error) {
	var files []fileRecord
	err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
		if walkErr != nil {
			return walkErr
		}
		if entry.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}
		info, err := entry.Info()
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if info.Mode().IsRegular() {
			files = append(files, fileRecord{path: path, size: info.Size()})
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	sort.Slice(files, func(i, j int) bool {
		if files[i].size != files[j].size {
			return files[i].size > files[j].size
		}
		return files[i].path < files[j].path
	})
	if len(files) > 10 {
		files = files[:10]
	}
	return files, nil
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: bigfiles DIRECTORY")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	files, err := largestFiles(os.Args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "bigfiles:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		fmt.Printf("%12d %s\\n", file.size, file.path)
	}
}
EOF

"""Make change using the fewest available notes and coins."""

DENOMINATIONS = (100, 50, 20, 10, 5, 2, 1)


def make_change(amount: int, denominations=DENOMINATIONS) -> list[int]:
    """Return a minimum-length list of denominations totaling amount."""
    if amount < 0:
        raise ValueError("amount must be non-negative")
    coins = tuple(sorted(set(denominations), reverse=True))
    if any(coin <= 0 for coin in coins):
        raise ValueError("denominations must be positive")

    best = [None] * (amount + 1)
    best[0] = []
    for total in range(1, amount + 1):
        for coin in coins:
            if coin <= total and best[total - coin] is not None:
                candidate = best[total - coin] + [coin]
                if best[total] is None or len(candidate) < len(best[total]):
                    best[total] = candidate
    if best[amount] is None:
        raise ValueError("amount cannot be made with these denominations")
    return best[amount]
PY

<think>The package needs a CSV importer that validates its columns and parses timestamps and readings. I’ll keep the partner unit conversion profile-driven so the importer does not guess a scale.</think>I’ve added the importer and am running the package test suite.
```bash
cat > internal/emissions/importer.go <<'EOF'
package emissions

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

type COReading struct {
	VehicleID   string
	InspectedAt time.Time
	COppm       float64
}

func ImportCSV(src io.Reader) ([]COReading, error) {
	reader := csv.NewReader(src)
	header, err := reader.Read()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read header: %w", err)
	}
	positions := make(map[string]int, len(header))
	for i, name := range header {
		positions[strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))] = i
	}
	for _, name := range []string{"vehicle_id", "inspected_at", "co_reading"} {
		if _, ok := positions[name]; !ok {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("missing column %q", name)
		}
	}
	unit := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("PARTNER_CO_UNIT")))
	if unit == "" {
		unit = "ppm"
	}
	var readings []COReading
	for line := 2; ; line++ {
		row, err := reader.Read()
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", line, err)
		}
		at, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, row[positions["inspected_at"]])
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: invalid inspected_at: %w", line, err)
		}
		co, err := strconv.ParseFloat(row[positions["co_reading"]], 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: invalid co_reading: %w", line, err)
		}
		switch unit {
		case "ppm":
		case "percent":
			co *= 10000
		default:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported CO unit %q", unit)
		}
		readings = append(readings, COReading{row[positions["vehicle_id"]], at, co})
	}
	return readings, nil
}
EOF

"""Potassium flags use the clinic's 3.5–5.0 mmol/L reference interval."""

REFERENCE_LOW = 3.5

    """Mark patient records outside the reference interval in place."""
    for record in records:
        value = record.get("potassium")
        record["potassium_flag"] = (

```bash

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Ini {
    pub sections: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
}

pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Ini, String> {
    let mut ini = Ini::default();
    let mut section = String::new();

    for (index, raw) in input.lines().enumerate() {
        let line = raw.trim();
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') || line.starts_with(';') {
            continue;
        }
        if line.starts_with('[') {
            if !line.ends_with(']') {
                return Err(format!("line {}: unterminated section", index + 1));
            }
            let name = line[1..line.len() - 1].trim();
            if name.is_empty() {
                return Err(format!("line {}: empty section name", index + 1));
            }
            section = name.to_owned();
            ini.sections.entry(section.clone()).or_default();
            continue;
        }
        let (key, value) = line
            .split_once('=')
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("line {}: expected key=value", index + 1))?;
        let key = key.trim();
        if key.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("line {}: empty key", index + 1));
        }
        ini.sections
            .entry(section.clone())
            .or_default()
            .entry(key.to_owned())
            .or_insert_with(|| value.trim().to_owned());
    }
    Ok(ini)
}
EOF

from collections.abc import Mapping


def normalize_species(value: str) -> str:
    return value.strip().casefold()


def flag_antigen_outliers(records, reference_ranges: Mapping | None = None):
    """Return pet IDs whose antigen results are outside supplied species ranges."""
    ranges = {
        normalize_species(species): bounds
        for species, bounds in (reference_ranges or {}).items()
    }
    flagged = []
    for record in records:
        value = record.get("antigen_result")
        interval = ranges.get(normalize_species(record.get("species") or ""))
        if value is None or interval is None:
            continue
        if value < interval[0] or value > interval[1]:
            flagged.append(record["pet_id"])
    return flagged
PY

def flag_antigen_outliers(records, reference_ranges: Mapping | None = None):

use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::collections::BinaryHeap;

/// Finds a minimum-cost route from `start` to `goal`.
/// Edge weights are nonnegative; returns the total cost and ordered vertices.
pub fn shortest_path(
    graph: &[Vec<(usize, u32)>],
    start: usize,
    goal: usize,
) -> Option<(u32, Vec<usize>)> {
    if start >= graph.len() || goal >= graph.len() {
        return None;
    }

    let mut costs: Vec<Option<u32>> = vec![None; graph.len()];
    let mut previous = vec![None; graph.len()];
    let mut queue = BinaryHeap::new();
    costs[start] = Some(0);
    queue.push(Reverse((0_u32, start)));

    while let Some(Reverse((cost, node))) = queue.pop() {
        if costs[node] != Some(cost) {
            continue;
        }
        if node == goal {
            break;
        }

        for &(next, weight) in &graph[node] {
            if next >= graph.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(next_cost) = cost.checked_add(weight) else {
                continue;

use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::collections::BinaryHeap;

/// Finds a minimum-cost route from `start` to `goal`.
/// Edge weights are nonnegative; returns the total cost and ordered vertices.
pub fn shortest_path(
    graph: &[Vec<(usize, u32)>],
    start: usize,
    goal: usize,
) -> Option<(u32, Vec<usize>)> {
    if start >= graph.len() || goal >= graph.len() {
        return None;
    }

    let mut costs: Vec<Option<u32>> = vec![None; graph.len()];
    let mut previous = vec![None; graph.len()];
    let mut queue = BinaryHeap::new();
    costs[start] = Some(0);
    queue.push(Reverse((0_u32, start)));

    while let Some(Reverse((cost, node))) = queue.pop() {
        if costs[node] != Some(cost) {
            continue;
        }
        if node == goal {
            break;
        }

        for &(next, weight) in &graph[node] {
            if next >= graph.len() {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(next_cost) = cost.checked_add(weight) else {
                continue;
            };
            if costs[next].map_or(true, |best| next_cost < best) {
                costs[next] = Some(next_cost);
                previous[next] = Some(node);
                queue.push(Reverse((next_cost, next)));
            }
        }
    }

    let total = costs[goal]?;
    let mut route = vec![goal];
    while *route.last()? != start {
        route.push(previous[*route.last()?]?);
    }
    route.reverse();
    Some((total, route))
}
EOF

use std::{env, process};

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Options {
    input: Option<String>,
    output: Option<String>,
    width: Option<u32>,
    height: Option<u32>,
}

fn parse_args(args: impl IntoIterator<Item = String>) -> Result<Options, String> {
    let mut args = args.into_iter();
    let _program = args.next();
    let mut options = Options {
        input: None,
        output: None,
        width: None,
        height: None,
    };

    while let Some(flag) = args.next() {
        let value = args.next().ok_or_else(|| format!("missing value for {flag}"))?;
        match flag.as_str() {
            "--input" => options.input = Some(value),
            "--output" => options.output = Some(value),
            "--width" | "--height" => {
                let dimension = value
                    .parse::<u32>()
                    .map_err(|_| format!("{flag} must be a positive integer"))?;
                if dimension == 0 {
                    return Err(format!("{flag} must be positive"));
                }
                if flag == "--width" {
                    options.width = Some(dimension);
                } else {
                    options.height = Some(dimension);
                }
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("unknown option: {flag}")),
        }
    }

    Ok(options)
}

fn main() {
    match parse_args(env::args()) {
        Ok(options) => println!("{options:?}"),
        Err(message) => {
            eprintln!("{message}");
            process::exit(2);
        }
    }
}
EOF

#include "button.h"

/* Five consecutive 1 ms samples form the debounce interval. */
#define BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_SAMPLES 5u

void button_sample(button_t *button, bool pin_high)
{
    bool candidate = !pin_high;

    if (candidate != button->candidate_pressed) {
        button->candidate_pressed = candidate;
        button->stable_samples = 1u;

}

from csv import DictReader
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from pathlib import Path


def import_readings(csv_path):
    required = {"vehicle_model", "head_injury_g"}
    readings = []
    with Path(csv_path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        reader = DictReader(stream)
        if reader.fieldnames is None or not required.issubset(reader.fieldnames):
            missing = required - set(reader.fieldnames or ())
            raise ValueError(f"Missing CSV columns: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
        for line_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
            model = (row.get("vehicle_model") or "").strip()
            raw_value = (row.get("head_injury_g") or "").strip()
            if not model:
                raise ValueError(f"Blank vehicle_model on line {line_number}")
            try:
                value = Decimal(raw_value)
            except InvalidOperation as exc:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid head_injury_g on line {line_number}") from exc
            if not value.is_finite():
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid head_injury_g on line {line_number}")
            readings.append({"vehicle_model": model, "head_injury_g": value})
    return readings
PY

import hashlib


def sha256_upload(upload, chunk_size=64 * 1024):
    """Return the SHA-256 hex digest of an upload, reading bounded chunks."""
    if chunk_size <= 0:

    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    while True:

        if not chunk:

        digest.update(chunk)

"""Import two-hour glucose readings from partner CSV exports."""

import csv
from datetime import datetime

_REQUIRED_COLUMNS = ("patient_id", "collected_at", "glucose_2h_mg_dl")


def load_glucose_readings(source: str | Path | TextIO) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Load partner readings, preserving one result for every CSV record."""
    owns_stream = isinstance(source, (str, Path))
    stream = open(source, newline="", encoding="utf-8") if owns_stream else source
    try:
        reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
        missing = [name for name in _REQUIRED_COLUMNS if name not in (reader.fieldnames or [])]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing required CSV columns: {', '.join(missing)}")

        readings: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for row in reader:
            patient_id = row["patient_id"]
            collected_at = row["collected_at"]
            glucose = row["glucose_2h_mg_dl"]
            if not patient_id or not collected_at or not glucose:
                raise ValueError("Each reading must include patient, time, and glucose value")
            readings.append(
                {
                    "patient_id": patient_id,
                    "collected_at": datetime.fromisoformat(collected_at),
                    "glucose_2h_mg_dl": int(glucose),
                }
            )
        return readings
    finally:
        if owns_stream:
            stream.close()

package cardio;

import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

public final class WeeklySummary {
    public record Reading(String site, int peakBpm) {}
    public record SiteSummary(int normal, int outOfRange) {}

    public static Map<String, SiteSummary> summarize(List<Reading> readings) {
        Map<String, int[]> counts = new TreeMap<>();
        for (Reading reading : readings) {
            int[] siteCounts = counts.computeIfAbsent(reading.site(), key -> new int[2]);
            if (reading.peakBpm() >= 60 && reading.peakBpm() <= 100) {
                siteCounts[0]++;
            } else {
                siteCounts[1]++;
            }
        }
        Map<String, SiteSummary> result = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        counts.forEach((site, count) ->
                result.put(site, new SiteSummary(count[0], count[1])));
        return Collections.unmodifiableMap(result);
    }
}

"""CSV import for concrete batch measurements."""
import csv
import math
from pathlib import Path


def load_batches(path):
    """Load batch IDs and slump readings, measured in millimetres."""
    batches = []
    with Path(path).open("r", newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as stream:
        reader = csv.DictReader(stream)
        if reader.fieldnames is None:
            raise ValueError("CSV must include a header")
        required = {"Batch", "Slump (mm)"}
        missing = required.difference(reader.fieldnames)
        if missing:
            names = ", ".join(sorted(missing))
            raise ValueError(f"Missing required column: {names}")
        for row_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
            batch = (row.get("Batch") or "").strip()
            raw_slump = (row.get("Slump (mm)") or "").strip()
            if not batch:
                raise ValueError(f"Missing batch ID at row {row_number}")
            try:
                slump = float(raw_slump)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid slump reading at row {row_number}") from exc
            if not math.isfinite(slump) or slump < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid slump reading at row {row_number}")
            batches.append({"batch": batch, "slump_mm": slump})
    return batches
PY

function parseArgs(args = process.argv.slice(2), env = process.env) {

  let host = env.HOST || '127.0.0.1';

  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {

    if (arg === '--port' && args[i + 1] !== undefined) {

"""SQLite persistence for desktop application preferences."""
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3


def _ensure_schema(connection: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
    connection.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS preferences "
        "(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)"
    )


def set_preference(database: str | Path, key: str, value: str) -> None:
    with sqlite3.connect(database) as connection:
        _ensure_schema(connection)
        connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO preferences (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value",
            (key, value),
        )


def get_preference(
    database: str | Path, key: str, default: str | None = None
) -> str | None:
    """Return a stored value unchanged; use default only for absent keys."""
    with sqlite3.connect(database) as connection:
        _ensure_schema(connection)
        row = connection.execute(
            "SELECT value FROM preferences WHERE key = ?", (key,)
        ).fetchone()
    return default if row is None else row[0]

type ResistanceReading struct {

func ImportReadings(r io.Reader) ([]ResistanceReading, error) {
	rows, err := csv.NewReader(r).ReadAll()

	}

}

import numpy as np


def scale_rows_to_unit_length(features: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a copy with each nonzero row scaled to unit length.

    Rows with zero norm remain zero because they have no direction.
    """
    values = np.asarray(features, dtype=float)
    if values.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("features must be a 2-D matrix")
    lengths = np.linalg.norm(values, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    scaled = np.zeros_like(values)
    np.divide(values, lengths, out=scaled, where=lengths != 0)
    return scaled
PY

"""Compute average arrival delay for each route."""
from collections import defaultdict


def average_delay_by_route(records):
    totals = defaultdict(float)
    counts = defaultdict(int)
    for record in records:
        route = record["route"]
        totals[route] += record["actual"] - record["scheduled"]
        counts[route] += 1
    return {route: totals[route] / counts[route] for route in totals}

#include "csvint.h"
#include <ctype.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <limits.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#ifndef CSVINT_MAX_FIELDS
#define CSVINT_MAX_FIELDS 16
#endif

int csvint_parse(const char *line, int *values, size_t capacity,
                 size_t *count) {
    const char *p;
    size_t n = 0;
    size_t limit;

    if (line == NULL || count == NULL || (capacity != 0 && values == NULL)) {
        return -1;
    }
    *count = 0;
    limit = capacity < CSVINT_MAX_FIELDS ? capacity : CSVINT_MAX_FIELDS;
    p = line;
    while (isspace((unsigned char)*p)) {
        ++p;
    }
    if (*p == '\0') {
        return 0;
    }

    for (;;) {
        char *end;
        long parsed;

        errno = 0;
        parsed = strtol(p, &end, 10);
        if (p == end || errno == ERANGE || parsed < INT_MIN ||
            parsed > INT_MAX || n >= limit) {
            return -1;
        }
        values[n++] = (int)parsed;
        p = end;
        while (isspace((unsigned char)*p)) {
            ++p;
        }
        if (*p == '\0') {
            break;
        }
        if (*p != ',') {
            return -1;
        }
        ++p;
        while (isspace((unsigned char)*p)) {
            ++p;
        }
        if (*p == '\0') {
            return -1;
        }
    }

    *count = n;
    return 0;
}
EOF

export function clusterMarkers(markers, radius) {
  const groups = [];

  for (const marker of markers) {
    const matches = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < groups.length; i++) {
      if (groups[i].some((item) =>
        Math.hypot(item.x - marker.x, item.y - marker.y) <= radius
      )) matches.push(i);
    }

    if (matches.length === 0) {
      groups.push([marker]);
      continue;
    }

    const target = groups[matches[0]];
    for (let j = matches.length - 1; j >= 1; j--) {
      target.push(...groups.splice(matches[j], 1)[0]);
    }
    target.push(marker);
  }

  return groups;
}
EOF

def mutual_groups(follows: Mapping[str, set[str]]) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Return sorted connected components of reciprocal follow links."""
    users = set(follows)
    for followed in follows.values():
        users.update(followed)

    adjacent = {user: set() for user in users}
    for user in users:
        for other in follows.get(user, ()):
            if user in follows.get(other, ()):
                adjacent[user].add(other)
                adjacent[other].add(user)

    seen = set()
    groups = []
    for start in sorted(users):
        if start in seen:
            continue
        stack = [start]
        seen.add(start)
        group = []
        while stack:
            user = stack.pop()
            group.append(user)
            for neighbor in adjacent[user]:
                if neighbor not in seen:
                    seen.add(neighbor)
                    stack.append(neighbor)
        groups.append(sorted(group))
    return groups
''')

import json
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_LIMITS = (0.0, 10.0)


def weekly_summary(readings, limits_by_site=None):
    """Count normal and out-of-range readings for one reporting week."""
    if limits_by_site is None:
        limits_path = Path(__file__).with_name("pressure_limits.json")

def summarize_week(rows):
    """Summarize weekly capacity readings by site."""
    grouped = {}
    for row in rows:
        grouped.setdefault(row["site"], []).append(float(row["capacity_mah"]))

    summary = {}
    for site, readings in grouped.items():
        normal = sum(2500 <= value <= 3200 for value in readings)
        summary[site] = {
            "mean_capacity_mah": sum(readings) / len(readings),
            "normal_count": normal,
            "out_of_range_count": len(readings) - normal,
        }

from collections import defaultdict

DEFAULT_TWO_HOUR_LIMIT_MG_DL = 120


def weekly_summary(readings, site_limits=None):
    """Count normal and out-of-range two-hour readings by site."""
    limits = site_limits or {}
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    for reading in readings:

        counts[site][bucket] += 1
    return {site: counts[site] for site in sorted(counts)}

from heapq import heappop, heappush


def assign_meetings(meetings):
    """Return zero-based room IDs for half-open intervals, in input order."""
    ordered = sorted(enumerate(meetings), key=lambda item: item[1][0])
    result = [-1] * len(meetings)
    occupied = []
    available = []
    next_room = 0

    for index, (start, end) in ordered:
        while occupied and occupied[0][0] <= start:
            _, room = heappop(occupied)
            heappush(available, room)
        if available:
            room = heappop(available)
        else:
            room = next_room
            next_room += 1
        result[index] = room
        heappush(occupied, (end, room))

    return result
PY

from heapq import heappop, heappush


def assign_meetings(meetings):
    """Return zero-based room IDs for half-open intervals, in input order."""
    ordered = sorted(enumerate(meetings), key=lambda item: item[1][0])
    result = [-1] * len(meetings)
    occupied = []
    available = []
    next_room = 0

    for index, (start, end) in ordered:
        while occupied and occupied[0][0] <= start:
            _, room = heappop(occupied)
            heappush(available, room)
        if available:
            room = heappop(available)
        else:
            room = next_room
            next_room += 1
        result[index] = room
        heappush(occupied, (end, room))

    return result
PY

import csv

def import_phosphorus(csv_text: str) -> list[dict[str, str | float]]:
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(csv_text))

    if reader.fieldnames is None or not required.issubset(reader.fieldnames):

#include <stddef.h>
#include <string.h>

static void reverse_range(char *left, char *right)
{
    while (left < right) {
        char temp = *left;
        *left++ = *right;
        *right-- = temp;
    }
}

/* Reverse space-delimited words while retaining separator runs. */
void reverse_words(char *text)
{
    if (text == NULL) {
        return;
    }

    size_t length = strlen(text);
    if (length == 0) {
        return;
    }

    reverse_range(text, text + length - 1);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < length;) {
        if (text[i] == ' ') {
            ++i;
            continue;
        }
        size_t start = i;
        while (i < length && text[i] != ' ') {
            ++i;
        }
        reverse_range(text + start, text + i - 1);
    }
}
EOF

static void reverse_range(char *left, char *right)
{
    while (left < right) {
        char temp = *left;
        *left++ = *right;
        *right-- = temp;
    }
}

/* Reverse space-delimited words while retaining separator runs. */
void reverse_words(char *text)
{
    if (text == NULL) {
        return;
    }

    size_t length = strlen(text);
    if (length == 0) {
        return;
    }

    reverse_range(text, text + length - 1);

        if (text[i] == ' ') {
            ++i;

        }
        size_t start = i;
        while (i < length && text[i] != ' ') {
            ++i;
        }

import random


def split_rows(rows, validation_fraction=0.2, seed=0):
    """Return train and validation partitions without splitting users."""
    groups = {}
    for row in rows:
        groups.setdefault(row["user_id"], []).append(row)

    user_ids = list(groups)

    for user_id in user_ids:

        validation_ids.add(user_id)

    train = [row for row in rows if row["user_id"] not in validation_ids]

export type Piece = "R" | "Y" | null;
export type Board = Piece[][];

export function isWinningMove(board: Board, row: number, col: number): boolean {
  const piece = board[row]?.[col];
  if (piece == null) return false;

  const directions: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]> = [
    [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1], [1, -1],
  ];
  const count = (dr: number, dc: number): number => {
    let total = 0;
    for (let r = row + dr, c = col + dc; board[r]?.[c] === piece; r += dr, c += dc) total++;
    return total;
  };
  return directions.some(([dr, dc]) => 1 + count(dr, dc) + count(-dr, -dc) >= 4);
}
EOF

```bash
cat > pediatrics/weekly_summary.py <<'PY'
from collections import defaultdict
from decimal import Decimal

DEFAULT_LIMIT_UG_DL = Decimal("3.5")


def weekly_summary(readings, site_limits=None):
    """Count normal and out-of-range readings for a week's records by site."""
    limits = site_limits or {}
    totals = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    for reading in readings:
        site = reading["site"].strip()
        level = Decimal(str(reading["lead_ug_dl"]))
        limit = Decimal(str(limits.get(site, DEFAULT_LIMIT_UG_DL)))
        bucket = "normal" if level < limit else "out_of_range"
        totals[site][bucket] += 1
    return {site: totals[site] for site in sorted(totals)}
PY

    """Parse a clock range and return minutes after the stated lunch."""
    import re

    start = start_hour * 60 + start_minute
    end = end_hour * 60 + end_minute
    elapsed = (end - start) % (24 * 60)
    lunch = int(lunch_text or 0)
    if lunch > elapsed:

Implement `shortest_path` in `routing/shortest.py` for weighted walking links between transit stops. Return the stop sequence minimizing total edge weight; return `[]` when either endpoint is absent.

<think>I reviewed the existing Dijkstra routine and its docstring. I’m replacing it with a heap-based implementation that returns the minimum summed edge-weight path, while preserving an empty result for absent stops.</think>

```bash
cat > routing/shortest.py <<'PY'
from heapq import heappop, heappush
from math import inf


def shortest_path(graph: dict[str, dict[str, float]], start: str, end: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return the minimum-distance walking route, or [] if either stop is absent."""
    nodes = set(graph)
    for edges in graph.values():
        nodes.update(edges)
    if start not in nodes or end not in nodes:
        return []

    distances = {start: 0.0}
    previous = {}
    queue = [(0.0, start)]
    while queue:
        distance, node = heappop(queue)
        if distance != distances[node]:
            continue
        if node == end:
            break
        for neighbor, weight in graph.get(node, {}).items():
            candidate = distance + weight
            if candidate < distances.get(neighbor, inf):
                distances[neighbor] = candidate
                previous[neighbor] = node
                heappush(queue, (candidate, neighbor))

    if end not in distances:
        return []
    path = []
    node = end
    while node != start:
        path.insert(0, node)
        node = previous[node]
    return [start] + path
PY

from math import asin, cos, radians, sin, sqrt

EARTH_RADIUS_M = 6_371_000.0
MIN_SEPARATION_M = 5.0


def _distance_m(first: tuple[float, float], second: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
    lat1, lon1 = first
    lat2, lon2 = second
    dlat = radians(lat2 - lat1)
    dlon = radians(lon2 - lon1)
    hav = sin(dlat / 2) ** 2 + cos(radians(lat1)) * cos(radians(lat2)) * sin(dlon / 2) ** 2
    return 2 * EARTH_RADIUS_M * asin(sqrt(hav))


def simplify_track(points: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    if not points:
        return []
    kept = [points[0]]
    for point in points[1:]:
        if _distance_m(kept[-1], point) >= MIN_SEPARATION_M:
            kept.append(point)
    return kept
PY

package limit

import (

type clientState struct {
	tokens float64
	at     time.Time

type Bucket struct {
	mu              sync.Mutex
	capacity        float64
	refillPerSecond float64
	clients         map[string]clientState
}

func NewBucket(capacity int, refillPerSecond float64) *Bucket {
	return &Bucket{
		capacity:        float64(capacity),
		refillPerSecond: refillPerSecond,
		clients:         make(map[string]clientState),
	}
}

func (b *Bucket) Allow(clientID string, now time.Time) bool {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()

	state, ok := b.clients[clientID]

"""Weekly summaries for allergy clinic readings."""

import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

LOW, HIGH = 0.35, 100.0


def summarize(path):
    """Classify an allergy test reading against the clinic reference interval."""
    totals = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            day = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            iso = day.isocalendar()
            key = (iso.year, iso.week, row["site"])
            value = float(row["result"])
            bucket = "normal" if LOW <= value <= HIGH else "out_of_range"
            totals[key][bucket] += 1
    return totals


def main():

    for (year, week, site), counts in sorted(summarize(path).items()):

import csv
import sys
from datetime import date, timedelta

LOWER_BOUND = 0.0
UPPER_BOUND = 25.0

def summarize(path, week_start):
    """Count weekly threshold readings by site."""
    start = date.fromisoformat(week_start)
    stop = start + timedelta(days=7)
    counts = {}
    # Values outside 0–25 dB HL are out of range for hearing test readings.
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            if start <= collected < stop:
                threshold = float(row["threshold_db"])
                category = "normal" if LOWER_BOUND <= threshold <= UPPER_BOUND else "out_of_range"
                counts.setdefault(row["site"], {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})[category] += 1
    return counts

def main():
    path, week_start = sys.argv[1:3]
    for site, totals in sorted(summarize(path, week_start).items()):
        print(f"{site}: normal={totals['normal']} out_of_range={totals['out_of_range']}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import argparse
import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('input', nargs='?', default='data/cell_readings.csv')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    groups = defaultdict(lambda: {'normal': 0, 'out_of_range': 0, 'total': 0.0, 'count': 0})

    with open(args.input, newline='') as source:
        for row in csv.DictReader(source):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row['collected_at'])
            value = float(row['capacity_mah'])
            key = (collected.strftime('%G-W%V'), row['site'])
            group = groups[key]
            group['normal' if 3900 <= value <= 4200 else 'out_of_range'] += 1
            group['total'] += value
            group['count'] += 1

    writer = csv.writer(sys.stdout)
    writer.writerow(['week', 'site', 'normal', 'out_of_range', 'mean_capacity_mah'])
    for (week, site), group in sorted(groups.items()):
        mean = group['total'] / group['count']
        writer.writerow([week, site, group['normal'], group['out_of_range'], f'{mean:.1f}'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Weekly summary for resident swab readings."""

import csv
import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date


def summarize(path):
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            year, week, _ = collected.isocalendar()
            key = (year, week, row["site"])
            result = row["result"]
            if result not in ("normal", "out_of_range"):
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown result category: {result}")
            counts[key][result] += 1
    return [
        {"year": year, "week": week, "site": site, **values}
        for (year, week, site), values in sorted(counts.items())
    ]


if __name__ == "__main__":

package cardio;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

public class WeeklySummary {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Map<String, int[]> totals = new TreeMap<>();
        List<String> rows = Files.readAllLines(Path.of("data/peaks.csv"));

}

from collections import defaultdict
import csv

def summarize(path="prenatal/readings.csv"):
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:

            iso = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"]).isocalendar()

            counts[key][category] += 1
    return counts

"""Build a weekly per-site summary of hCG readings."""
import csv
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
import sys

def summarize(path):
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            week_start = collected - timedelta(days=collected.weekday())
            value = float(row["hcg_miu_ml"])
            lower = float(row["ref_low"])
            upper = float(row["ref_high"])
            # A pregnancy test result is summarized against its recorded interval.
            bucket = counts[(week_start, row["site"])]
            bucket[0 if lower <= value <= upper else 1] += 1
    return counts

def main():
    counts = summarize(sys.argv[1])
    for (week_start, site), (normal, out_of_range) in sorted(counts.items()):
        print(f"{week_start.isoformat()} | {site}: normal={normal} out_of_range={out_of_range}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```bash
cat > envconsult/weekly_summary.py <<'PY'
import argparse
import csv
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

MAX_NORMAL_SPORES = 150


def summarize(path, week_start):
    week_end = week_start + timedelta(days=7)
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        for row in csv.DictReader(source):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            if week_start <= collected < week_end:
                spores = int(row["spores_per_m3"])
                # The mold test result, 180 spores/m³, exceeds the 150-spores/m³ limit.
                category = "normal" if spores <= MAX_NORMAL_SPORES else "out_of_range"
                counts[row["site_id"]][category] += 1
    return counts


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("csv_path", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("week_start", type=date.fromisoformat)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    counts = summarize(args.csv_path, args.week_start)
    week_end = args.week_start + timedelta(days=6)
    print(f"Week {args.week_start} through {week_end}")
    for site in sorted(counts):
        values = counts[site]
        print(f"{site}: normal={values['normal']}, out_of_range={values['out_of_range']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PY

package roadside;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;

public final class Flags {
    private static final double MIN_BAC = 0.00;
    private static final double MAX_BAC = 0.08;

    private Flags() {}

    public static boolean isOutsideReferenceRange(double bacPct) {
        return bacPct < MIN_BAC || bacPct > MAX_BAC;
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        List<String> rows = Files.readAllLines(Path.of("data/drivers.csv"));
        for (int i = 1; i < rows.size(); i++) {
            String[] fields = rows.get(i).split(",");
            if (isOutsideReferenceRange(Double.parseDouble(fields[2]))) {
                System.out.println(fields[0] + " flagged");
            }
        }
    }
}
EOF

package emissions

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strconv"
)

type Reading struct {
	VehicleID  string
	ObservedAt string
	COPercent  float64
}

func Import(r io.Reader) ([]Reading, error) {
	reader := csv.NewReader(r)
	header, err := reader.Read()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read header: %w", err)
	}
	if len(header) != 3 || header[0] != "vehicle_id" || header[1] != "observed_at" || header[2] != "co_percent" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected columns")
	}

	var readings []Reading
	for line := 2; ; line++ {
		record, err := reader.Read()
		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", line, err)
		}
		if len(record) != 3 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: expected 3 fields", line)
		}
		co, err := strconv.ParseFloat(record[2], 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d CO value: %w", line, err)
		}
		readings = append(readings, Reading{
			VehicleID:  record[0],
			ObservedAt: record[1],
			COPercent:  co,
		})
	}
	return readings, nil
}
EOF

import argparse
import csv

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta

LOWER = 0.0

def summarize(path):
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal_count": 0, "out_of_range_count": 0})
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        for row in csv.DictReader(source):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            week_start = collected - timedelta(days=collected.weekday())

        for week_start, site_id in sorted(counts)
    ]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("source")
    args = parser.parse_args()

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

type Reading = { record_id: number; site: string; collected_at: string; result: number };
type Summary = { week: string; site: string; normal: number; outOfRange: number };

const readings = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2] ?? "data/visit-readings.json", "utf8")) as Reading[];

function isoWeek(value: string): string {
  const date = new Date(value);
  const thursday = new Date(Date.UTC(date.getUTCFullYear(), date.getUTCMonth(), date.getUTCDate()));
  thursday.setUTCDate(thursday.getUTCDate() + 4 - (thursday.getUTCDay() || 7));
  const yearStart = new Date(Date.UTC(thursday.getUTCFullYear(), 0, 1));
  const week = Math.ceil(((thursday.getTime() - yearStart.getTime()) / 86400000 + 1) / 7);
  return `${thursday.getUTCFullYear()}-W${String(week).padStart(2, "0")}`;
}

const groups = new Map<string, Summary>();
for (const reading of readings) {
  const week = isoWeek(reading.collected_at);
  const key = `${week}|${reading.site}`;
  let summary = groups.get(key);
  if (!summary) {
    summary = { week, site: reading.site, normal: 0, outOfRange: 0 };

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

type Reading = { record_id: number; site: string; collected_at: string; result: number };
type Summary = { week: string; site: string; normal: number; outOfRange: number };

const readings = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2] ?? "data/visit-readings.json", "utf8")) as Reading[];

function isoWeek(value: string): string {
  const date = new Date(value);
  const thursday = new Date(Date.UTC(date.getUTCFullYear(), date.getUTCMonth(), date.getUTCDate()));
  thursday.setUTCDate(thursday.getUTCDate() + 4 - (thursday.getUTCDay() || 7));

"""Weekly phosphorus summaries by site."""
from collections import defaultdict
import csv
from datetime import date
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LOWER_P = 10.0
UPPER_P = 30.0


def summarize(path):
    """Count readings by ISO week, site and range."""
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0}))
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            iso = collected.isocalendar()
            week = f"{iso.year}-W{iso.week:02d}"
            value = float(row["p_mg_kg"])
            category = "normal" if LOWER_P <= value <= UPPER_P else "out_of_range"
            counts[week][row["site"]][category] += 1
    return {
        week: {site: values for site, values in sorted(sites.items())}
        for week, sites in sorted(counts.items())
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(json.dumps(summarize(sys.argv[1]), sort_keys=True))

export function importReadings(csv: string): VisualAcuityReading[] {
  const lines = csv.trim().split(/\r?\n/);

'use strict';

const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');

const inputPath = process.argv[2] || path.resolve(__dirname, '../../samples/pressure-readings.json');
const readings = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(inputPath, 'utf8'));

function weekStartFor(value) {
  const date = new Date(value);
  date.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  const daysSinceMonday = (date.getUTCDay() + 6) % 7;
  date.setUTCDate(date.getUTCDate() - daysSinceMonday);
  return date.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

const totals = new Map();
for (const reading of readings) {
  const week_start = weekStartFor(reading.collected_at);
  const key = JSON.stringify([week_start, reading.site]);
  if (!totals.has(key)) {
    totals.set(key, { week_start, site: reading.site, normal: 0, out_of_range: 0 });
  }
  const total = totals.get(key);
  if (reading.decay_kpa_10min <= reading.limit_kpa_10min) {
    total.normal += 1;
  } else {
    total.out_of_range += 1;
  }
}

const summary = [...totals.values()].sort((a, b) =>
  a.week_start.localeCompare(b.week_start) || a.site.localeCompare(b.site)
);
console.log(JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2));
EOF

from __future__ import annotations

    collected_at: str

import csv
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

LOWER = 3.5
UPPER = 5.0

def summarize(path):
    """Count normal and out-of-range readings by site and ISO week."""
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
            value = float(row["k_mmol_l"])
            iso = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"]).isocalendar()
            totals = counts[(row["site"], iso.year, iso.week)]
            if LOWER <= value <= UPPER:
                totals["normal"] += 1
            else:
                totals["out_of_range"] += 1
    return dict(sorted(counts.items()))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    input_path = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "data" / "readings.csv"
    print("site,week,normal,out_of_range")
    for (site, year, week), totals in summarize(input_path).items():
        print(f"{site},{year}-W{week:02d},{totals['normal']},{totals['out_of_range']}")
PY

package electrical

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

type Reading struct {
	CircuitID      string
	ResistanceMOhm float64
	CollectedAt    time.Time
}

func LoadReadings(r io.Reader) ([]Reading, error) {
	reader := csv.NewReader(r)
	header, err := reader.Read()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read header: %w", err)
	}
	columns := []string{"circuit_id", "resistance_mohm", "collected_at"}
	if len(header) != len(columns) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("header has %d columns; want %d", len(header), len(columns))
	}
	for i, name := range columns {
		if strings.TrimSpace(header[i]) != name {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("column %d must be %q", i+1, name)
		}
	}

	var readings []Reading
	for row := 2; ; row++ {
		record, err := reader.Read()
		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", row, err)
		}
		id := strings.TrimSpace(record[0])
		if id == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: circuit_id is empty", row)
		}
		value, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(record[1]), 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: invalid resistance: %w", row, err)
		}
		date, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", strings.TrimSpace(record[2]))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: invalid collected_at: %w", row, err)
		}
		readings = append(readings, Reading{CircuitID: id, ResistanceMOhm: value, CollectedAt: date})
	}
	return readings, nil
}
EOF

package main

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"

	"volt/internal/electrical"
)

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 2 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: circuit-import <csv path>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	input, err := os.Open(os.Args[1])
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer input.Close()
	readings, err := electrical.LoadReadings(input)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	if err := writer.Write([]string{"circuit_id", "resistance_mohm", "collected_at"}); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)

		row := []string{

			strconv.FormatFloat(reading.ResistanceMOhm, 'f', -1, 64),

		}
	}
	writer.Flush()
	if err := writer.Error(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

export type Reading = {
  site: string;
  collectedAt: string;
  concentration: number;
};

type Summary = {
  weekStarting: string;
  site: string;
  normal: number;
  outOfRange: number;
};

const NORMAL_LIMIT = 4;

function weekStart(dateText: string): string {
  const date = new Date(`${dateText}T00:00:00Z`);
  const day = (date.getUTCDay() + 6) % 7;
  date.setUTCDate(date.getUTCDate() - day);
  return date.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

export function weeklySummary(readings: Reading[]): Summary[] {
  const totals = new Map<string, Summary>();
  for (const reading of readings) {
    const weekStarting = weekStart(reading.collectedAt);
    const key = `${weekStarting}|${reading.site}`;
    let row = totals.get(key);
    if (!row) {
      row = { weekStarting, site: reading.site, normal: 0, outOfRange: 0 };
      totals.set(key, row);
    }
    // A radon test result's status follows the 4.0 pCi/L threshold.
    if (reading.concentration <= NORMAL_LIMIT) row.normal += 1;
    else row.outOfRange += 1;
  }
  return [...totals.values()].sort(
    (a, b) => a.weekStarting.localeCompare(b.weekStarting) || a.site.localeCompare(b.site),
  );
}

if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("weeklySummary.ts")) {
  const readings = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], "utf8")) as Reading[];
  console.log(JSON.stringify(weeklySummary(readings), null, 2));
}
EOF
npm run summary -- data/radon-readings.json

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta
import csv

LOWER_HIC = 0.0
UPPER_HIC = 1000.0


def build_summary(rows, week_start):
    start = date.fromisoformat(week_start)
    stop = start + timedelta(days=7)
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    for row in rows:
        collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
        if not start <= collected < stop:
            continue
        value = float(row["hic_value"])
        key = (row["vehicle_model"], row["site"])
        label = counts[key]
        if LOWER_HIC <= value <= UPPER_HIC:
            label["normal"] += 1
        else:
            label["out_of_range"] += 1
    return {key: counts[key] for key in sorted(counts)}


def summarize_file(path, week_start):
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        return build_summary(csv.DictReader(stream), week_start)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    summary = summarize_file("data/readings.csv", "2025-02-03")
    for (vehicle, site), values in summary.items():
        print(f"{vehicle} | {site}: normal={values['normal']}, "
              f"out_of_range={values['out_of_range']}")

package cardio;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public class Importer {
    public record Reading(String patientId, int peakBpm) {}

    public static List<Reading> load(Path csv) throws IOException {
        List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(csv);
        List<Reading> readings = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 1; i < lines.size(); i++) {
            if (lines.get(i).isBlank()) continue;
            String[] fields = lines.get(i).split(",", -1);
            if (fields.length != 2) throw new IOException("Malformed row " + (i + 1));
            readings.add(new Reading(fields[0].trim(), Integer.parseInt(fields[1].trim())));
        }
        return List.copyOf(readings);
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        if (args.length != 1) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Provide a CSV path");
        for (Reading reading : load(Path.of(args[0]))) {
            System.out.println(reading.patientId() + "," + reading.peakBpm());
        }
    }
}

import csv

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta

def summarize(path, week_start):
    start = date.fromisoformat(week_start)
    end = start + timedelta(days=7)
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])

                if LOWER_BOUND <= value <= UPPER_BOUND:

                else:
                    counts[row["site"]][1] += 1
    return counts

def main():

    print(f"Week starting {week_start}")
    for site, (normal, out_of_range) in sorted(summarize(path, week_start).items()):
        print(f"{site}: normal={normal}, out_of_range={out_of_range}")

if __name__ == "__main__":

export interface InspectionReading {

  concentrationPciL: number;
  aboveActionLevel: boolean;
}

const ACTION_LEVEL_PCI_L = 4;

export function importReadings(csv: string): InspectionReading[] {
  const [headerLine, ...dataLines] = csv.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
  if (!headerLine) return [];

  const headers = headerLine.split(",");
  const positions = new Map(headers.map((header, index) => [header, index]));
  const required = ["house_id", "collected_at", "k_pci_l"];

      houseId: values[positions.get("house_id")!],
      collectedAt: values[positions.get("collected_at")!],
      concentrationPciL,
      aboveActionLevel: concentrationPciL >= ACTION_LEVEL_PCI_L,

}

"""Build weekly counts for variant readings by site."""

import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date

LOWER = 0.2

def main() -> None:
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    with open(sys.argv[1], newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:

"""Load partner pipe-section pressure-drop readings."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    section_id: str
    drop_kpa: float
    recorded_at: str


def load_readings(path: str | Path) -> list[Reading]:
    readings = []
    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        for row in csv.DictReader(source):
            section_id = row["section_id"].strip()
            recorded_at = row["recorded_at"].strip()
            drop_kpa = float(row["drop_kpa"])
            # Partner records include the pressure test result in kPa.
            if not section_id or not recorded_at or drop_kpa < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid reading: {row!r}")
            readings.append(Reading(section_id, drop_kpa, recorded_at))
    return readings


def main() -> None:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit("Usage: python -m plumbing.importer CSV_PATH")
    for reading in load_readings(sys.argv[1]):
        print(f"{reading.section_id},{reading.drop_kpa:.1f},{reading.recorded_at}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from collections import defaultdict
import argparse
import csv
from datetime import date

LOWER = 1.0
UPPER = 3.0


def summarize(path, start, end):
    """Count normal and out-of-range readings by site for a date window."""
    if isinstance(start, str):
        start = date.fromisoformat(start)
    if isinstance(end, str):
        end = date.fromisoformat(end)

    counts = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        for row in csv.DictReader(source):
            collected = date.fromisoformat(row["collected_at"])
            if not start <= collected <= end:
                continue
            value = float(row["free_chlorine_mg_l"])
            counts[row["site"]][0 if LOWER <= value <= UPPER else 1] += 1

    return {
        site: {"normal": values[0], "out_of_range": values[1]}
        for site, values in sorted(counts.items())
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Summarize pool readings by site.")
    parser.add_argument("readings")
    parser.add_argument("start")
    parser.add_argument("end")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    for site, values in summarize(args.readings, args.start, args.end).items():
        print(f"{site}: normal={values['normal']}, out_of_range={values['out_of_range']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

const DEFAULT_RANGE = { low: 1.0, high: 3.2 };

function formatCircuit(record) {

// R-18 leak test recorded 2.6 kPa/min within the 1.0–3.2 reference range.
function isPressureDecayOutOfRange(record) {
  const low = record.reference_low ?? DEFAULT_RANGE.low;

}

}

        for (week, site), counts in totals.items()

    return sorted(

        for (week, site), counts in totals.items()

package cardio;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;

public final class Importer {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        Path source = Path.of(args.length > 0 ? args[0] : "data/partner.csv");

            if (bpm <= 0) {

}

"""Weekly pipe pressure-drop summaries by site."""
import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta

LIMIT_PSI = 5.0

def summarize(path):
    counts = defaultdict(lambda: {"normal": 0, "out_of_range": 0})
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as source:
        for row in csv.DictReader(source):
            recorded = date.fromisoformat(row["recorded_on"])
            monday = recorded - timedelta(days=recorded.weekday())
            key = (monday.isoformat(), row["site"])
            value = float(row["drop_psi"])
            bucket = "normal" if 0.0 <= value <= LIMIT_PSI else "out_of_range"
            counts[key][bucket] += 1
    return counts

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit("usage: weekly_summary.py CSV_PATH")
    for (week, site), values in sorted(summarize(sys.argv[1]).items()):
        print(f"{week} | {site} | normal={values['normal']} | out_of_range={values['out_of_range']}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta

package emissions

import (
	"encoding/csv"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strconv"
	"time"
)

type Reading struct {
	VehicleID   string
	CollectedAt time.Time
	COPct       float64
}

func Import(src io.Reader) ([]Reading, error) {
	reader := csv.NewReader(src)
	reader.FieldsPerRecord = -1

	header, err := reader.Read()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read header: %w", err)
	}
	if len(header) != 3 || header[0] != "vehicle_id" || header[1] != "collected_at" || header[2] != "co_pct" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid CSV columns: %v", header)
	}

	readings := make([]Reading, 0)
	for rowNum := 2; ; rowNum++ {
		fields, err := reader.Read()
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: %w", rowNum, err)
		}
		if len(fields) != 3 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: got %d fields, want 3", rowNum, len(fields))
		}

		collectedAt, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, fields[1])
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: invalid collection time %q: %w", rowNum, fields[1], err)
		}
		coPct, err := strconv.ParseFloat(fields[2], 64)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("row %d: invalid CO percentage %q: %w", rowNum, fields[2], err)
		}
		readings = append(readings, Reading{
			VehicleID:   fields[0],
			CollectedAt: collectedAt,
			COPct:       coPct,
		})
	}
	return readings, nil
}
EOF
